stories.title: Mahakumbh-style management at Kashi Vishwanath Dham during 'Sawan':No VIP Darshan allowed, devotees to enter through five routes
stories.summary: Preparations for Sawan (Shravan) have begun at Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi, with the temple administration making extensive arrangements in anticipation of millions of devotees during the holy month, which will be observed from 30 July to 28 August. This year, crowd management measures modelled on the Mahakumbh will be implemented to ensure the safety and convenience of pilgrims. Every Monday during Sawan, devotees will follow a five-route entry system, no-vehicle zones will be enforced, and mobile phone restrictions will remain in place. The temple administration has also announced that there will be no VIP darshan on any Monday during Sawan. To assist elderly and specially-abled devotees, e-rickshaw services will be provided, while the entire temple complex will be monitored through CCTV surveillance, additional security personnel and newly introduced Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Auspicious yogas on the first monday of Sawan The first Monday of Sawan in 2026 falls on 3 August, a day regarded as highly significant in the Hindu calendar. It coincides with Panchami Tithi of Shravan Krishna Paksha. According to astrological calculations, the day will also witness the influence of Uttarabhadrapada and Revati Nakshatra. In addition, Sukarma Yoga and Dhriti Yoga will be in effect, making the occasion especially auspicious. Throughout Sawan, Baba Vishwanath will be adorned in different forms every Monday. This year's decorations will include- E-Rickshaws for elderly and specially-abled Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Shambhu Sharan said mobile phones will be completely prohibited inside the Kashi Vishwanath Dham complex during Sawan. No devotee will be permitted to enter the temple carrying a mobile phone. Officials said the measure will strengthen security, improve crowd management and help devotees remain focused on worship. Every Monday during Sawan, the stretch between Maidagin and Godaulia will be declared a no-vehicle zone. The temple administration will operate e-rickshaw services for elderly, disabled and infirm devotees from Godaulia to Gate No. 4 and Maidagin to Gate No. 4. No VIP darshan on Sawan Mondays Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal said comprehensive security and crowd management plans are being finalised in view of the expected arrival of lakhs of devotees throughout Sawan. He said the objective is to ensure devotees receive darshan smoothly and within a shorter waiting time while avoiding long queues. Authorities are working on all aspects of entry and exit arrangements, barricading and crowd control. Existing CCTV cameras have been reviewed, and additional cameras will be installed wherever required. Deployment points for the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), paramilitary forces and the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) are also being identified. The Police Commissioner reiterated that no VIP protocol will be applicable on any Monday during Sawan. stories.title: Storms and rain in 20 UP cities, alert in 75:Lightning strike kills 7; monsoon set to arrive within 24 hours
stories.summary: The weather system responsible for the onset of the southwest monsoon has become active over Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in 20 cities across the state on Tuesday morning. Rainfall was recorded in Kanpur Nagar, Ayodhya, Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Deoria, Sitapur, Bahraich, Pilibhit, Gonda, Raebareli, Lalitpur, Chitrakoot, Farrukhabad, Jaunpur, Kanpur Dehat, Unnao, Rampur and Moradabad. Heavy rain causes waterlogging, strong winds uproot trees Heavy rainfall in Deoria and Jaunpur led to waterlogging in agricultural fields. In Gorakhpur, strong winds uprooted trees, which fell onto roads. Raebareli witnessed thunderstorms, rain and lightning. Cloudy skies prevailed across the rest of the state, bringing significant relief from the heat, with brief spells of sunshine in between. Thunderstorm and heavy rain alert issued for all 75 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rainfall alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. Heavy rainfall is likely in 38 districts, while lightning is also expected at isolated places. According to the IMD, the impact of the ongoing heatwave is expected to end from Tuesday, and the southwest monsoon could enter Uttar Pradesh at any time within the next 24 hours. Agra hottest in the state during the past 24 hours Over the past 24 hours, Agra recorded the highest temperature in the state at 42.9°C. Rainfall was reported in 15 cities, including Lucknow. In Firozabad, strong winds caused a tree to fall onto an e-rickshaw, killing five people and injuring three others. Meanwhile, lightning strikes claimed the lives of a woman in Basti and a nine-year-old child in Maharajganj. Monsoon expected to arrive around 10 days late According to the IMD, the southwest monsoon has remained stalled along the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar border for the past 19 days, but is expected to advance further on Tuesday. Once it enters the state, the first spell of heavy rainfall is likely to affect the Terai region, including Kushinagar, Maharajganj and Siddharthnagar. The monsoon typically reaches Uttar Pradesh by 20 June, but this year it is advancing around 10 days behind schedule. Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said- The monsoon is currently advancing via Motihari in Bihar. Pre-monsoon activity and light rainfall have already begun in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Terai region. From tomorrow, or between 1 and 5 July, both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh are likely to witness widespread heavy rainfall. Temperatures are expected to drop by as much as 10°C.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to get eastern UP's first NCC Training Academy:₹47.88 crore project to be completed in three months
stories.summary: The construction of Eastern Uttar Pradesh’s first state-of-the-art National Cadet Corps (NCC) Training Academy is expected to be completed within the next three months, by September 2026. The academy is being developed over a 10-acre site at Tal Kandla in Gorakhpur. A major initiative of the Yogi government, the academy is set to become a landmark institution for NCC training in the region. The project is being built at a cost of Rs 47.88 crore. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for the academy at Tal Kandla, Gorakhpur, on 9 March 2024. Construction began in June 2024 and is scheduled for completion by September 2026. The project is being executed by Construction and Design Services, Jal Nigam, Unit-42, Gorakhpur, at a total cost of Rs 47.88 crore. According to Vivek Gupta, Project Manager of the executing agency, more than 75 per cent of the construction work has been completed. The structural work on both the administrative building and hostels has been finished, while interior finishing work is currently in progress. Facilities at the NCC training academy The academy will feature a comprehensive range of modern training and residential facilities, including- In addition, infrastructure worth Rs 7.17 crore will be developed, including the construction of a boundary wall, sentry posts on all sides, guard rooms and high-mast floodlights. Eleven districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh to benefit The NCC Group Gorakhpur, which operates under the motto "Unity and Discipline", oversees NCC activities across 11 districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh- To train cadets from affiliated universities, schools and colleges, the group organises an average of 25 to 30 Combined Annual Training Camps (CATCs), Army Camps, Inter-Group Competitions, Republic Day Parade training programmes, and a range of social service activities every year. Notably, the National Cadet Corps (NCC) is the world's largest uniformed youth organisation, dedicated to instilling the values of unity, discipline and national service among young people.

stories.title: Man stabs friend to death in Varanasi:Dispute over dancing at wedding turns fatal; crowd beats accused
stories.summary: A young man was fatally stabbed by his own friend during a dispute while dancing to a DJ at a wedding ceremony in Varanasi on Monday night. The seriously injured victim was first taken to Jakhini Government Hospital, where he received first aid before being referred to the BHU Trauma Centre because of the severity of his injuries. The incident sparked tension in the village. Angry villagers assaulted the accused after the attack, while women and other residents later protested against the police when officers returned to the village. A heavy police presence has since been deployed in the area. The incident took place under the Mirzamurad police station limits. Argument during DJ dance turns violent According to police, a wedding ceremony was being held at the home of Ramesh Gaud, a resident of Lalpur (Ledui) village. After the groom's procession arrived, a DJ performance was underway at the Janwasa (guest accommodation for the groom's party) in Khagrampur. During the celebrations, 24-year-old Rohit Rajbhar and Anshu Vishwakarma, both residents of the village, were dancing when an argument broke out between them. The dispute quickly escalated. Police said Anshu allegedly pulled out a knife he was carrying and stabbed Rohit in the chest. Villagers catch and beat the accused Rohit collapsed to the ground, bleeding heavily, triggering panic at the wedding venue. Villagers and wedding guests present at the scene caught Anshu Vishwakarma as he attempted to flee and assaulted him before police arrived. After receiving information about the incident, officers from Mirzamurad Police Station reached the spot, rescued the accused from the crowd and took him into custody. Meanwhile, Rohit was taken to Jakhini Government Hospital by ambulance. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the BHU Trauma Centre, where he later succumbed to his injuries. Heavy police deployment after village protest The stabbing created a tense atmosphere in the village. When police returned to the village later, angry women and other residents staged a protest and forced the police team to leave the area. In view of the tension, the administration has deployed additional police personnel in the village. Police said the investigation is underway and security arrangements have been strengthened to maintain law and order.

stories.title: Police escort UP Congress chief for Ram Mandir ‘darshan’ post-house-arrest:Officers grill 'chanda chor' accused inside jail
stories.summary: The political controversy surrounding the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Mandir intensified on Tuesday after Uttar Pradesh Congress President Ajay Rai was allowed to offer prayers at the Ram Mandir around 9 pm, nearly 20 hours after being placed under house arrest. Police had detained Rai late Monday night to prevent a proposed protest by a Congress delegation over the alleged donation theft. Images of his temple visit had not surfaced at the time of reporting. Ajay Rai detained ahead of planned protest Police placed Ajay Rai under house arrest at an Ayodhya hotel around 11:30 pm on Monday before shifting him to the guest house of Narendra Dev University of Agriculture and Technology, nearly 50 km from the Ram Mandir. Rai was leading a Congress delegation that had announced a protest outside the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust office over the alleged donation theft. The delegation also included Congress MPs Kishori Lal Sharma, Tanuj Punia, and Ujjwal Raman Singh, all of whom were also placed under house arrest. Congress workers detained during March At around 12:30 pm on Tuesday, Congress workers attempted to march towards the Ram Janmabhoomi temple. Police stopped them at Tedhi Bazar, nearly one kilometre from the temple, leading to a confrontation. As workers allegedly tried to push through the barricades, police used mild force and detained several protesters before taking them away in police vehicles. Ajay Rai's wife alleges political vendetta Earlier in the day, Ajay Rai's wife, Reena Rai, released a video statement from Varanasi, accusing the BJP government of trying to suppress her husband's voice. She alleged that after taking him away in a police vehicle, authorities deliberately misled their associates about his whereabouts. Reena Rai also said the Congress would continue its campaign against those allegedly involved in the donation theft and warned that the government would be responsible if any harm came to her husband.

stories.title: UP govt offers interest-free loans:Young entrepreneurs can access funding of up to ₹1 crore for businesses
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is offering a range of subsidised loan schemes to help young entrepreneurs, women, farmers and businesses start or expand their ventures. Under different state and Central government schemes, eligible applicants can access interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh, low-interest agricultural loans, and business finance worth up to ₹1 crore, depending on the category. Here's a detailed look at the schemes, eligibility criteria and benefits. Interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh for young entrepreneurs Under the Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Yojana, eligible young entrepreneurs can obtain an interest-free and collateral-free loan of up to ₹5 lakh to start a business. The first loan, available on the initial application, must be repaid within four years. In addition, the government provides a 10% subsidy on the project cost. For example, if a business project costs ₹10 lakh, the government will contribute up to ₹1 lakh. Entrepreneurs who repay their first loan on time become eligible for a second loan of up to ₹10 lakh. Under this phase, borrowers pay only 3.5% interest for three years on loans of up to ₹7.5 lakh. Eligibility Applicants must- For further information, applicants can contact 9129-987-111 or email cmyuva.msme@gmail.com. Women can access loans of up to ₹20 lakh without collateral Women's Self-Help Groups (SHGs) with a good repayment record can obtain bank loans of up to ₹20 lakh without mortgaging land or property. The scheme is linked to the Central government's Lakhpati Didi Yojana, which aims to increase the annual income of women to more than ₹1 lakh. Women receive training in fields including- Initially, Self-Help Groups receive a revolving fund of ₹20,000-₹30,000. For example, if a group of ten women receives ₹30,000, the group can lend money to members to purchase livestock, sewing machines, or other income-generating assets. As the group's performance improves, it becomes eligible for a Community Investment Fund of up to ₹2.5 lakh, enabling members to jointly establish businesses such as dairy farms or spice-processing units. Well-performing groups can subsequently receive bank loans of up to ₹20 lakh. Products manufactured by these groups are marketed through platforms including Amazon Saheli, Flipkart Samarth, and GeM. Affordable loans for OBC and minority women The UP Backward Classes Welfare Department provides financial assistance to OBC and minority women under the Mahila Samriddhi Yojana. Eligible women can receive loans of up to ₹1.40 lakh to establish businesses such as- The annual interest rate ranges between 4% and 5%. Applications are processed through the office of the District Backward Classes Welfare Officer and Vikas Bhawan. Farmers can borrow up to ₹5 lakh at an effective interest rate of 4% Under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme, farmers can obtain low-cost loans for agriculture, livestock farming and fisheries. Banks generally charge 9% interest. However- According to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, farmers can obtain agricultural loans of up to ₹2 lakh without mortgaging land or other property. The government has also increased the subsidised KCC loan limit to ₹5 lakh, providing additional financial support. Special Agricultural loans under Mukhmantri Krishak Samridhi Yojana The Mukhmantri Krishak Samridhi offers cheaper loans through Cooperative Rural Development Banks. Previously, these loans carried interest of around 11.5%. Under the revised scheme, eligible farmers pay only 6% interest, with the state government subsidising the remaining amount. The concessional rate applies only to farmers who repay on time. Banks may impose penal interest on delayed repayments. Women farmers receive an additional 1% interest concession. The loans can be used to purchase- Borrowers can repay the loan over a period of up to 15 years. Eligibility The scheme is available only to- Applicants must not be loan defaulters. Farmers can apply through their nearest Cooperative Rural Development Bank branch. Government loan schemes for larger businesses Loans of up to ₹25 lakh for manufacturing and service businesses Under the Mukhyamantri Yuva Swarozgaar Yojana, entrepreneurs can obtain- Interest rates are charged according to standard bank norms. Funding pattern General category applicants Reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC, women, persons with disabilities and ex-servicemen) Applicants must- Capital subsidies of up to ₹4 crore for new industrial units Under the UP MSME Promotion Policy 2022, entrepreneurs establishing new industries receive extensive financial support. Capital subsidy For industries established in Bundelkhand and Purvanchal- For Madhyanchal and Paschimanchal- Women and SC/ST entrepreneurs receive an additional 2% subsidy. For example, a ₹50 lakh investment in a small industrial unit eligible for 20% subsidy would receive ₹10 lakh in government assistance. Additional incentives The policy also provides- ODOP scheme offers loans of up to ₹25 lakh Under the One District One Product (ODOP) scheme, entrepreneurs can obtain bank loans of up to ₹25 lakh, along with capital subsidies. Subsidy structure- The District Industries Centre (DIC) also assists entrepreneurs in securing bank finance. As the earlier odopup.in portal is no longer functional, applicants must now apply through the MSME portal, selecting the ODOP Margin Money Scheme and uploading the required documents. Women entrepreneurs can obtain loans of up to ₹1 crore Under the Stand-Up India Scheme, women and SC/ST entrepreneurs can access loans ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore to establish new businesses. The scheme does not require applicants to mortgage land or property. Entrepreneurs contribute only 10-15% of the project cost, while banks finance the remainder. The repayment period extends to seven years, with a moratorium of up to 18 months. Loans of up to ₹2 crore are available without collateral, while the government also bears the cost of the credit guarantee. Entrepreneurs can avail themselves of the scheme for up to 25 separate projects at different locations.

stories.title: Monsoon stalled at Bihar border for 19 days:Rainfall remains weak; lack of weather system delays showers in UP until July
stories.summary: The wait for the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh is finally expected to end. According to meteorologists, the monsoon is likely to reach Purvanchal and central Uttar Pradesh by July 1-2. Earlier, forecasts had suggested rainfall between June 20 and 25, but the monsoon system originating over the Bay of Bengal remained stalled along the Bihar border for the past 19 days. The absence of a low-pressure area over Uttar Pradesh primarily caused the delay. Weather experts say the monsoon operates through a chain reaction, and this crucial process did not develop as expected. Why did the monsoon get stuck? How a low-pressure system triggers rainfall Monsoon rainfall depends on the formation of a low-pressure area. When intense heat warms the land and surrounding air, the hot air becomes lighter and rises. This creates a low-pressure vacuum near the surface. To fill this vacuum, moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal rush inland. As these cool, humid winds move over the plains, they form rain-bearing clouds and trigger widespread rainfall. What happened this year This year, Uttar Pradesh failed to develop a sufficiently strong low-pressure system to draw the monsoon winds inland. As a result, the moisture-laden winds slowed considerably and remained stalled near the Bihar border instead of advancing into the state. Monsoon stalled, yet rainfall remains poor The monsoon is currently stalled around Motihari (East Champaran) in Bihar and along the Daltonganj line near the Jharkhand-Bihar border. Interestingly, even the districts where the monsoon has stalled have not received significant rainfall. According to the India Meteorological Department, wind patterns began changing on the evening of June 29. Heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds of 50-60 km/h has been forecast across Bihar and Jharkhand, including Motihari and Daltonganj. Meteorologists believe this weather system will push the stalled monsoon forward, allowing it to enter Uttar Pradesh within the next 24 to 48 hours. June rainfall and July-August forecast June recorded a severe rainfall deficit June proved to be exceptionally dry across Uttar Pradesh. A severe rainfall deficit was recorded in 34 districts, with the state's average rainfall about 60% below normal. Eastern Uttar Pradesh Western Uttar Pradesh July and August may also receive below-normal rain According to Skymet's Long Period Average (LPA) forecast, monsoon rainfall across Uttar Pradesh during July and August is expected to remain slightly below normal. Meteorologists say the influence of El Niño is strengthening once again over the Pacific Ocean. Its impact has slowed the movement of monsoon winds across Uttar Pradesh. Overall monsoon rainfall is expected to be around 90% to 94% of the Long Period Average, placing it in the below-normal category. July outlook The first half of July is expected to bring widespread monsoon rainfall across Purvanchal, Central Uttar Pradesh and Western Uttar Pradesh, providing relief after the prolonged delay. However, monsoon activity may weaken slightly during the second half of the month. Overall, July rainfall is expected to remain about 5% below normal. August outlook The monsoon is expected to weaken further during August, with rainfall likely to remain up to 8% below normal. This could prove particularly significant for Kharif crops, especially paddy, which depend heavily on adequate rainfall during this period. Records broken by June's extreme heat Heatwaves in Uttar Pradesh usually last only two to three days during June. This year, however, the delayed arrival of the monsoon resulted in severe heatwave conditions persisting for 10 to 14 days across nearly two-thirds of the state's districts. Normally, heatwave conditions subside around June 20-22 with the arrival of moisture-laden easterly winds. This year, they continued until June 30, leading to two major weather records. 1. Hottest night in 127 years Daytime temperatures in June typically range between 38°C and 40°C. This year, the mercury climbed to 47.6°C, while night-time temperatures reached 30.8°C, around 5°C to 8°C above normal. In Prayagraj, the minimum temperature on the night of June 11-12 reached 34.3°C, breaking a 127-year-old record. The previous highest night temperature, 33.5°C, was recorded in 1898. 2. UP districts among the world's hottest During June, Uttar Pradesh featured three times in global real-time temperature rankings. In the second week of June, 19 Indian cities were listed among the 20 hottest places in the world. Five districts from Uttar Pradesh featured in that list, Banda, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Mirzapur and Fatehpur. Meanwhile, Kanpur recorded maximum temperatures exceeding 47°C on multiple occasions. Why was the heat so severe? Delayed monsoon and absence of weather systems The monsoon reached Kerala four days later than usual before stalling near the Bihar border for nearly 19 days. This prolonged the spell of dry, hot weather by around eight additional days. At the same time, Uttar Pradesh did not experience any significant weather systems capable of triggering pre-monsoon rainfall. Clear skies allowed intense solar radiation to heat the land continuously, while dry westerly winds blowing from the deserts of Rajasthan and Pakistan kept temperatures exceptionally high across the state. Advice for farmers As widespread monsoon rainfall is expected during the first fortnight of July, farmers are advised to complete delayed paddy transplantation by July 15. With below-normal rainfall forecast for August, farmers should not rely entirely on the monsoon. Greater use of tube wells, borewells and canal irrigation is likely to be necessary, increasing the overall cost of cultivation.

stories.title: Bus crashes into trailer on Yamuna Expressway, 4 killed:27 passengers injured, SSP says, 'Conductor was driving the vehicle'
stories.summary: A Volvo bus crashed into the rear of a trailer on the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura at around 3:30 am on Tuesday, leaving four people dead and 27 passengers injured. The impact was so severe that the front section of the bus became lodged nearly eight feet inside the trailer. Several passengers were trapped inside the wreckage, while the body of one young man was left hanging out of a window. The accident took place in the Raya police station area, around 20 km from the Mathura district headquarters. The bus was travelling from Lucknow to Delhi with 65 passengers on board. Passengers rescued after windows and doors were broken open The collision triggered panic and chaos at the scene. Passengers were rescued by breaking open the bus windows and doors. Police, assisted by local residents, immediately launched a rescue operation. According to officials, 34 passengers escaped unhurt and were later sent to their destinations on other buses. Driver, conductor, cleaner and 1 passenger killed Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shlok Kumar said the victims included- The identities of three of the deceased have not yet been established. Rescue operation lasted nearly two hours Most passengers were asleep when the crash occurred. The force of the impact threw several people between the seats, leaving them trapped inside the mangled bus. Rescue teams used gas cutters to cut through the vehicle and free the trapped passengers. The rescue operation continued for nearly two hours. SSP Shlok Kumar said- Preliminary investigation suggests that the regular driver was not behind the wheel at the time of the accident. Instead, the conductor was driving the bus. The bus was travelling at high speed while the trailer was in its own lane. The conductor suddenly swerved the bus, causing it to crash into the rear of the trailer. See photos- How the accident unfolded ? SP (Rural) Suresh Chandra Rawat said the accident took place around 2 km before the Raya cut on the Yamuna Expressway. A trailer loaded with gravel (registration number RJ 47 GA 8143) was travelling in its designated lane when a speeding Gola Bus Service Volvo coach (registration number BR 28P 4723) approached from behind, lost control and rammed into it. The collision was so forceful that the front of the coach was crushed by 2 to 2.5 metres (around 8 feet). Police received information about the crash at 3:35 am, following which eight Police Response Vehicles (PRVs) and 12 ambulances were dispatched to the scene. A green corridor was created to ensure the injured could be transported to hospital without delay. SP Rawat said all the injured are receiving treatment and their condition is currently stable. The preliminary investigation indicates that driver negligence and overspeeding were the primary causes of the accident. Passengers escaped through the emergency exit Preeti Srivastava, a resident of Faridabad, said she was travelling from Lucknow to Faridabad with her husband and two children. She said the coach was travelling at a high speed and had stopped at a roadside eatery about 30 minutes before the accident. Shortly after resuming the journey, the vehicle began swerving. Many passengers were asleep when the crash occurred. "The passengers were thrown from their seats. People broke the glass of the emergency exit at the rear of the coach to rescue those trapped inside. We were later taken to hospital by ambulance," she said. Some injured referred to Agra, three in serious condition Dr Sushil Kumar of the Mathura District Hospital said 24 injured passengers had been brought to the hospital following the accident. Some of the injured have been referred to Agra for specialised treatment, while others from Delhi are also being transferred for further medical care. He said two to three patients remain in a serious condition, suffering fractures to the thigh bone (femur). The condition of the remaining injured passengers is stable.

stories.title: Violence after child dies in accident:Tractor-trolley set ablaze; police drive away protesters after lathi-charge
stories.summary: In Aligarh on Thursday, a 14-year-old boy died after being crushed under a tractor-trolley. This sparked anger among the people. They placed the body on the road and blocked traffic. They set fire to the tractor-trolley loaded with wheat. Firefighters who arrived after receiving information brought the fire under control. Police tried to pacify the protesting people. However, the family members remained adamant on their demand for compensation of one crore rupees and arrest of the accused driver. Police officers had to face opposition from the people. However, as the commotion escalated, police dispersed the crowd. The incident occurred at 4:10 PM in Chandaus town, about 35 km away from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as Vansh Pratap (14), son of Kalicharan. See 5 pictures Now know the sequence of events in detail... The deceased boy was studying in 8th grade Vansh, a resident of Elampura village in Aligarh, was an 8th-grade student. He had come to the nearby Chandaus town on a bike with his cousin brother around three o'clock on Thursday afternoon to get samosas. After getting the samosas packed, both brothers were returning to the village. At 4:10 PM on the Chandaus-Pisawa road, near Khair Adda, the bike suddenly skidded. Vansh came under the rear wheel of a tractor-trolley loaded with wheat that was moving alongside, resulting in his death on the spot. Meanwhile, his cousin brother also sustained minor injuries. Relatives adamant on demanding action As soon as the news of the accident reached the village, hundreds of people from the village along with family members reached the spot. Angered by Vansh's death, people set the tractor-trolley on fire. Within moments, the trolley started burning. Due to the arson and protest, a chaotic situation developed at the scene. As soon as the information was received, the Kotwali police, administrative officers, and fire brigade team reached the spot. However, the angry crowd prevented the police from lifting the body and the fire brigade from extinguishing the fire. For a long time, police officers tried to convince the people, but they remained adamant on their demand for action. Uncle said - Ambulance arrived two hours later Vansh's uncle Arjun Singh said - The ambulance did not reach the spot until about two hours after the incident. How did heavy and overloaded vehicles reach the area where no-entry is enforced. The police take bribes and allow heavy vehicles to come and go in the no-entry zone. The accident occurred due to police negligence. A fair investigation of this entire matter should be conducted. The guilty police personnel should be identified and strict action should be taken against them. Tension in the area, heavy police force deployed After the incident, there was a tense atmosphere in Chandaus town. Considering the situation, additional police force was called to the spot. The police kept trying to pacate people and normalize the situation. Meanwhile, SP City Aditya Bansal and CO Gabhana Mahesh Kumar reached the spot. They assured appropriate action on all demands of the family members. After this, around quarter past seven in the evening, the family members handed over the body to the police. The police took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem.

stories.title: ‘No offerings, no votes for BJP’:Akhilesh Yadav dares BJP to hold polls in September
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference on Thursday afternoon at around 3:30 PM in Lucknow. During this, he raised questions on the role of the government and trust regarding the Ram Mandir donation controversy. He said - Ram Mandir was forcibly occupied. No account was given of the donations coming to the temple. Despite complaints, the police took no action. He also claimed that the UP assembly elections should be held in September instead of November. We are fully prepared. SP has never broken and will never break. During this, Harishankar Safariwala, the Panch Pramukh of Ayodhya's 'Mandir Ram Niwas', was also present. Along with this, Akhilesh also cornered the government on law and order, cybercrime, expressway quality, and the 2027 assembly elections. Read the major statements made by Akhilesh SP is the only party that has not split Akhilesh Yadav said- Samajwadi Party is the only party that has not split till date. BJP has betrayed both the Constitution and God. They betrayed the Constitution, they betrayed God. When the public learns the truth about donation theft, they will remove them from power in the assembly elections and they will be wiped out. If the government is serious about corruption, then bulldozers should be run on the houses of the accused arrested in the Ram Temple donation theft case as well. Donations were stolen by turning off CCTV Akhilesh said that in a state where CCTV is turned off and temple offerings can be stolen, the increase in incidents like cyber fraud is not a big deal. This raises serious questions about the state's security system and surveillance mechanism. Lord Shri Ram himself will take account of this entire matter. The Samajwadi Party will continue to work towards building a nation of brotherhood and harmony. There is a poll in the news, you can participate before moving ahead The public should get an account of the offerings Akhilesh Yadav said - The allegations of irregularities in the offerings received in the name of Lord Ram are extremely serious. The complete account of devotees' donations should be made public. If there is no transparency even in matters related to faith, people's trust will be broken. The impact of this issue will also be visible in the elections. This time BJP will get neither donations, nor offerings, nor votes. We are ready for the 2027 elections If the government wants to hold the 2027 assembly elections before the scheduled time, the Samajwadi Party is fully prepared for it. Those who wanted to hold elections in November, let them hold them in September itself, we are ready. During the press conference, someone said that BJP people say that you are not a devotee of Ram. On this, Akhilesh said in an interesting manner - I am getting a temple built. From now on, whoever questions about God, I will collect donations from them for the temple. Police stations are working at the government's behest Akhilesh mentioned the murder of Sandeep Yadav in Siddharthnagar and an incident in Kaushambi. He said that the police in the state are not working impartially. Victims are not getting justice in many cases. There is political pressure on police stations. Cyber crimes are increasing rapidly in UP. In many cases, FIRs are not even registered and actual figures are not brought forward. Quality of expressway deteriorated due to corruption Referring to the Bundelkhand Expressway, Akhilesh said that flaws in the road came to light shortly after its inauguration. Quality is being compromised in development projects. Such situations are arising due to corruption. Farmers and Traders' Discontent in Ayodhya Became Reason for Defeat Referring to the Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh said that the discontent of farmers and traders in Ayodhya became a major reason for BJP's defeat. There was dissatisfaction among local people due to land acquisition for the airport and other projects and displacement of traders. Its impact was visible in the election results. Made Several Promises for Sikh Community In a press conference, Akhilesh Yadav said that when the Samajwadi Party government is formed, the Sikh community will be given proper representation in power and organization. He also promised to resolve land-related disputes, raise the issue of release of imprisoned Sikhs, and give priority to eligible Sikh candidates in elections. Akhilesh concluded by saying that SP will continue to struggle for democratic values and protection of the Constitution. It will continue to strongly raise public issues. Meanwhile, Harishankar Safariwala alleged that Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's General Secretary Champat Rai has occupied his historic temple. Safariwala claimed that the temple's donation money has also been withheld. He was lured with crores of rupees to suppress the matter. He tried to file a complaint with the police, but no action was taken. Business is being done in the name of religion and faith.

stories.title: Sanjay Nishad threatens party leader:‘Even your father will do the work’| WATCH
stories.summary: UP government's Cabinet Minister and Nishad Party's National President Dr. Sanjay Nishad reached Jalaun at 1:30 PM on Thursday. During the program here, he got angry at his state secretary. He reprimanded state secretary Bharat Lal right on the stage. He said, "Get your mind right, I will set your mind right, even your father will do the work." A video of the incident has surfaced. In the video, leaders and workers present nearby can be seen trying to mediate. Read the complete matter Dr. Sanjay Nishad had arrived on Thursday to attend a booth workers' conference at Shyam Palace in the Kalpi assembly constituency of Jalaun. During the conference, he was being welcomed. Meanwhile, around 1:45 PM, a dispute arose over the stage arrangements during the garland ceremony. State Secretary Bharat Lal suggested removing the women present on the stage. The minister got angry over this remark. He reprimanded Bharat Lal right from the stage. An argument began between the two. Seeing the situation deteriorate, leaders and workers present on the stage intervened to mediate. Bharat Lal said that he has been working for the party for a long time, but he is not getting opportunities according to his hard work. At this, Dr. Sanjay Nishad lost his temper. He said that work has to be done. Your father will also have to do it. Set your mind right... I will set your mind right. Party losing due to traitors Dr. Sanjay Nishad said that there were some seats where the party's victory was almost certain, but due to some traitors, the party had to face defeat. He claimed that he has a list of such people. Organizational action will be taken against them. Meanwhile, on the Ram Mandir donation issue in Ayodhya, the minister said that the government is keeping a serious watch on the entire matter. Investigation agencies are doing their work. If anyone is found guilty, strict action will be taken against them according to law. They will be sent to jail. Appeal to strengthen booths While addressing the conference, Dr. Sanjay Nishad appealed to the workers to strengthen the organization up to the booth level. He said that previous governments ignored the rights of the Nishad community. He called upon the workers to unite and fight for the rights of the community and engage in preparations for the assembly elections. State Secretary Bharat Lal said that the party's dedicated and active workers are being ignored. He alleged that tickets are given to outsiders, while those who have been working for the organization for years do not get a chance.

DSP Kamlesh Kant from Moradabad has been sent to Noida Commissionerate. Shiv Thakur from Saharanpur has been sent to Meerut. Manjari Rao has been made Deputy Superintendent of Police of Ballia. Shilpa Verma has been sent to Kannauj. Apart from this, Ashok Kumar Singh has been made DSP in Gorakhpur Railway from DSP Sant Kabir Nagar. Imran Khan has been appointed as Assistant Commandant in Prayagraj PAC from Lalitpur. Dharmendra Singh Yadav has been made DSP of Moradabad Police Academy from PAC Lucknow. Apart from this, changes have also been made in the Chief Minister's security. Sudhakar Dwivedi and Bhanu Pratap Singh from Lucknow Commissionerate have been deployed in the Chief Minister's security. stories.title: ₹3 crore rent, ₹200 crore scam:Fake call centre operated from luxury commercial tower In Lucknow; 119 people detained
stories.summary: A fake international call centre operating from Lucknow's Summit Building has been busted, exposing what police believe was a large-scale cyber fraud network targeting foreign nationals. The office, which reportedly cost nearly ₹3 crore a year to run, recruited employees through a five-stage interview process. When police received information that the operation was not a legitimate call centre but a cyber fraud hub, they raided the premises on Wednesday afternoon. The operation led to the detention of 119 people. Police also seized 100 laptops, 178 calling phones, digital devices and several documents. When Dainik Bhaskar visited the site after the raid, the office was locked, but the lavish interiors inside the hall reflected the scale of the operation. Family members of one employee reached the building soon after the raid. While they refused to speak on camera, they revealed that their son had cleared five interview rounds to get the job. Most employees were paid between ₹25,000 and ₹28,000 a month, but those involved in successful scams allegedly received a 10% commission from the amount defrauded. Here's how the gang allegedly operated, who worked there, how much they earned, how the racket was exposed, and how much money investigators believe has been siphoned off. See 2 pictures- Modus operandi of the fraudsters- The scamsters would become active at night According to preliminary police findings, the group was running an application called Dollar App under the guise of a call centre. Through it, callers allegedly lured victims from different countries and cheated them over the phone. The centre functioned primarily between 7 pm and 3 am, with overseas customers being the main targets. The accused had rented two offices on the 11th floor of Summit Building and were allegedly operating under the company name Solaris Solution. Mastermind sitting abroad would hire employees and get the work done During the raid, police detained Narayandas Khairajani, Lalit Khairajani from Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and Vikram Singh Parmar. Both Lalit and Parmar currently reside in Gomti Nagar Extension and were working as operation managers. Police believe they handled the India-based operations and supervised a large team of employees. Investigators are now questioning them to identify and reach the main mastermind, who is suspected to be operating from abroad. They would trap victims on refund processing or Google search Police say the fraudsters exploited online refund queries. People often search online for refund assistance after making purchases. Investigators claim that once a person searched for refund-related information, their details reached the fraudsters. The scammers would immediately call back, pose as customer support executives and guide victims through various processes. Eventually, they would obtain OTPs and gain access to bank accounts, siphoning off money. Working and Salary- Majority were girls from North-East Police sources say a significant number of employees were women from North-Eastern states. During questioning, many reportedly admitted they joined the company because of the promise of high earnings. Investigators believe their fluent English and neutral accents helped convince foreign nationals that they were speaking to genuine representatives. This, police say, made it easier to gain trust and execute the scams. Bonus was more than salary Employees at the call centre were required to communicate entirely in English. Their monthly salary ranged between ₹25,000 and ₹28,000, but the major attraction was the incentive structure. Workers allegedly received 10% of the amount recovered through fraud, which often exceeded their fixed pay. According to sources, some employees were earning between ₹80,000 and ₹1 lakh every month through commissions alone. Investigators also believe that most employees were aware that the operation involved fraudulent activities. Income and Expenditure- Defrauded more than 200 crore rupees Based on the evidence recovered, police suspect the network may have cheated foreign citizens out of more than ₹200 crore. Investigators say victims were trapped using different kinds of inducements and deceptive tactics. All electronic devices seized during the raid have been sent for forensic examination, while financial transactions and money trails are also being scrutinised. Sources claim the office occupied two sections of the building and incurred an annual expense of around ₹3 crore, including rent and operational costs. The call centre had reportedly been functioning for nearly a year. Officials believe the investigation began after complaints were received from overseas, eventually leading to the crackdown. All documents will be sent for forensics Crime branch officials said all recovered digital devices and documents have been taken into custody for technical and forensic analysis. The aim is to identify the broader cybercrime network, trace victims, understand the calling modules and uncover crucial evidence linked to financial transactions. ADCP Crime Kiran Yadav said the investigation is continuing and efforts are underway to arrest the remaining accused at the earliest.

stories.title: Mother files FIR against PCS officer daughter:Alleges ₹15 lakh black money deposited in her account, land mafia links
stories.summary: A case has been registered against five people, including a District Supply Officer (DSO) posted in Hapur, in Saharanpur. The FIR has been filed on the complaint of her mother. On 30 June, police registered the case under charges of cheating, forgery, criminal conspiracy and criminal intimidation. The complainant, the mother of the DSO, has alleged that her daughter used her bank account to hide “illicit income”. She claims that ₹15 lakh was deposited into her account without her permission or knowledge, and that there was an attempt to grab her land. She further alleges she was threatened with death when she objected. The case has been registered at Sarsawa police station. ‘My bank account was used without consent’, says mother Munesh Rani, a resident of Mirpur Sitapur village, said her daughter Seema had opened a bank account in her name at an ICICI Bank branch in Ghaziabad and operated it herself. She alleged that she was never informed about the transactions in the account. She came to know about the matter only after receiving a message on her mobile phone. When she checked at the bank, the details were confirmed. She further alleged that ₹15 lakh was deposited into her account by her daughter, and claimed it was done to conceal her daughter’s “illegal earnings”. Daughter accused of being part of land mafia gang The complainant has further alleged that her daughter is part of a land mafia gang. She claims Seema, along with Sanjeev Chaudhary and Gambhir from Mirpur Sitapur (Sarsawa), Rajendra Rana from Mirpura village in Baghpat, and Naresh Kumar from Pahlanpur village in Sarsawa, conspired to grab her land. She alleged that a forged receipt dated 16 September 2023 was created using fake signatures in an attempt to take over her property. She said she came to know about it through the tehsil administration. When she opposed the alleged attempt, she was threatened with death, she further claimed. She also said she was forced to sell her land to Nancy, a resident of Dehradun. She added that she first filed a complaint at Sarsawa police station on 13 May, but no action was taken. She later approached the SSP, after which the FIR was registered on 30 June around 4:30 pm against Seema Chaudhary and four others. Police say investigation underway Police have registered the case under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 506 of the IPC based on the complaint and have begun an investigation. Officials said a fair and impartial probe is underway, and the allegations will be verified during the investigation before any conclusion is reached.

stories.title: Lucknow Sahara City land battle escalates:270-acre green belt dispute reaches Supreme Court after 30 years
stories.summary: The long-running dispute over 270 acres of land developed as Sahara City in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar has now reached the Supreme Court. The Municipal Corporation claims that Sahara violated lease conditions by carrying out residential and commercial construction on land originally allotted for a green belt, and also says the 30-year lease period has expired. On the other hand, Sahara argues that it has invested ₹2,480 crore in the project and that the land was taken over without following due legal procedure. Meanwhile, the state government is preparing plans to build a new Assembly complex on the same land, with the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) assigned responsibility. The land was originally allotted by the Lucknow Municipal Corporation to Sahara India on a ₹100 stamp paper. The key question now is who has the legal right over this land. At present, the Municipal Corporation has taken possession, alleging breach of lease conditions. The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the matter on 31 July. 100-rupee lease that sparked a 270-acre dispute The dispute over 270 acres in Vipul Khand, Gomti Nagar, dates back nearly three decades. It began on 22 October 1994, when the Lucknow Municipal Corporation allotted the land to Sahara India Housing Limited through a licence deed executed on a ₹100 stamp paper. Under the agreement, the company was required to pay ₹1,000 per acre as a fee. The parcel included around 170 acres of Municipal Corporation land and 100 acres of LDA land. A key condition of the lease was that the entire area would be developed as a green belt. Petitioner advocate BK Singh alleges that the lease process itself was against rules from the beginning. According to him, allotting such a large parcel on a ₹100 stamp paper for 30 years did not comply with LDA regulations. After the completion of the 30-year period, the Municipal Corporation has alleged that the land was used for purposes contrary to the agreement and that lease conditions were violated. On this basis, in September 2025, the Corporation cancelled the lease and took possession of the land. 'Land was given to Sahara bypassing rules' In the ongoing legal battle, petitioner advocate B.K. Singh has consistently described the lease as illegal and against regulations. He says that in 1994–95, the Municipal Corporation and LDA bypassed rules while allotting the land to Sahara. No registered deed was executed; instead, the lease was granted on stamp paper with an annual rent of ₹1,000 per acre, which he claims was not as per prescribed procedures. According to him, the land was meant exclusively for green belt development under the master plan, but later commercial activities and construction began. He alleges that several structures within the complex violate lease conditions. Singh further says that instead of challenging these orders directly, the matter was prolonged through multiple litigations for years. He argues that the 30-year lease period has now ended, and no authority is obligated to renew it. He also cites a 2017 award by Justice Kamlesh Nath, stating that the matter linked to SEBI proceedings should be resolved first, but reiterates that no authority can be forced to extend a lease. He maintains that the land was never used for its intended purpose, and instead of a green belt, it was turned into a commercial zone. He adds that the High Court has also made observations in this regard. Singh claims Sahara has already failed to obtain relief from the Supreme Court in the past and argues that violation of lease terms gives the government full right to reclaim the land. He further says that Municipal Corporation is only a custodian of public property, while LDA should have strictly followed legal procedures during allotment. Municipal corporation’s stand: lease violations alleged The Municipal Corporation maintains that the land allotted for green belt development was gradually converted into residential and commercial use. According to the Corporation, luxury bungalows, a modern theatre, a 5,000-capacity auditorium, and even airport-like security arrangements were developed within the premises. It alleges that the original lease conditions were not followed and that about 40 acres were meant to remain reserved as green belt, but were diverted for other uses, violating land use regulations. Officials say several notices were issued in 2020 and again in 2025, but no corrective action was taken. The Corporation claims adequate opportunity was given to rectify violations, but compliance never followed. Land was to be used for Green Belt As per the lease deed, the land was to be used exclusively for developing a green belt in the city, with no commercial use permitted. Around 40 acres were to remain green area, and any construction was to follow LDA and Municipal Corporation rules. No deviation from land use norms was allowed, and all fees and conditions had to be followed regularly. The Municipal Corporation states that if lease conditions are violated, the lease can be terminated and possession of land can be taken back. It further claims the licence deed was terminated as early as 1997, followed by multiple notices, and formal action was taken in 2025. The LDA first cancelled the lease, followed by the Municipal Corporation’s action. How much money did Sahara pay to the Municipal Corporation and LDA in exchange for the land? Advocate B.K. Singh claims that the 270 acres were given on a ₹100 stamp paper. He says a land development agreement was made between the Municipal Corporation, LDA, and Sahara India, but the entire lease process was against rules. He also states that Sahara has claimed in court that it invested around ₹2,480 crore in the project and developed over 87 buildings. The company has also said it was willing to deposit additional funds for lease renewal if required. Sahara's petition was dismissed on April 22, 2026 The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court rejected Sahara’s petition on 22 April 2026. Following this, Sahara moved the Supreme Court through a Special Leave Petition (SLP). In its plea, Sahara referred to an arbitration order by retired Justice Kamlesh Nath and argued that it supported lease renewal considerations. Here is the English translation of the infographic detailing Sahara's arguments in the Supreme Court: What arguments did Sahara present in the Supreme Court? The 2017 arbitration order is in its favor: In September 2017, the decision in the mediation/arbitration case was ruled in favor of Sahara. The entire land is not a green belt: The company claims that the Municipal Corporation is taking action on wrong grounds by declaring the entire area a green belt. Crores of rupees were invested: Sahara states that it has spent approximately ₹2,480 crore (24.8 billion rupees) on the project. Principles of natural justice were not followed: Possession of the land was taken away without providing an adequate or fair opportunity to be heard. Were ready to extend the lease: If any fee or charges were required to be paid, the company was completely ready to deposit it. What has the Supreme Court asked? On 29 May 2026, a bench comprising Chief Justice Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi issued notices seeking responses from the government, Municipal Corporation and LDA. What grounds did the Municipal Corporation cite for canceling the lease? The Municipal Corporation says that constructions deviated from the original purpose, green belt conditions were violated, repeated notices were ignored, and lease conditions were not followed. 'No possession without compensation and legal process' Sahara has argued in the Supreme Court that thousands of crores were invested in the project and that the arbitration order of 2017 is in its favour. It claims the entire land is not a green belt and that the Municipal Corporation’s action is not legally valid. It further argues that possession cannot be taken without compensation and proper legal procedure. Now Eyes on July 31 The hearing scheduled for 31 July 2026 is considered crucial in this high-profile dispute. It is expected to determine whether control over the valuable land in Gomti Nagar will remain with Sahara or go to the government. The future of the proposed new Vidhan Sabha complex on this land will also largely depend on the Supreme Court’s decision.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl falls 15 feet to death:Feeding monkeys when one lunged at her; CCTV captures fatal fall
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the first floor of a building in Vrindavan on Wednesday evening. She was feeding monkeys from a window when one of the monkeys suddenly lunged at her. The sudden attack caused her to lose balance, and she fell nearly 15 feet onto the street below. The incident took place around 4:30 pm on Wednesday in the Banke Bihari police outpost area. The CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Thursday morning, showing the girl falling from the first floor. At the time of the accident, only her younger brother was at home, while her parents had gone to work. Locals rushed her to a hospital immediately, where doctors declared her dead. The deceased has been identified as Poorva (13), daughter of Anil Pandey, a resident of Sant Colony. Now, read what is visible in the CCTV CCTV footage shows a three-storey building with iron grills on the first-floor window, where the girl was feeding monkeys. A white car is seen parked in the lane below, and a young man is sitting outside the house. Suddenly, the girl is seen falling straight from the first floor onto the road. Hearing the sound, the man rushes outside, and within seconds a crowd gathers at the spot. See 3 pictures Family was at work, younger brother at home The girl’s father, Anil Pandey, lives with his wife, son, and adopted daughter Poorva in a rented first-floor accommodation in Sant Colony. The family originally hails from Ayodhya and earns a living by running a food cart near Parikrama Marg. Monkeys are frequently seen in the area. On Wednesday, both parents had left for work, leaving Poorva and her younger brother at home. Feeding monkeys turned fatal In the evening, Poorva was standing on a stool and feeding monkeys from the window when one of the monkeys suddenly attacked. She lost balance and fell from the first floor onto the street below. She suffered severe head injuries, and blood was seen on the road. Locals immediately informed her parents and rushed her to the hospital, but doctors declared her dead. Police also reached the spot and began an investigation. Police statement and final update Banke Bihari outpost in-charge Shiv Kumar Sharma said the girl died after falling from the first floor of the building. He added that she was mentally unwell. The family refused to take legal action, after which the body was handed over to them.

stories.title: SIT questions Ram Mandir trustee Anil Mishra behind closed doors:Demolition of two donation theft accused’s homes planned
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) is questioning Ram Mandir trustee Dr Anil Mishra in a closed room inside the Ayodhya temple complex in connection with the alleged donation theft case. Invited trust member Gopal Rao has been asked to wait outside while the questioning continues. The development comes after SIT questioned trust General Secretary Champat Rai for nearly three hours on Sunday. Investigators are now questioning Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao to cross-check his statements. The probe is focused on their alleged role in the appointment of accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The SIT reached the temple at around 3 pm on Thursday. Earlier, the team had conducted an extensive investigation between 15 and 20 June. Meanwhile, Ayodhya Police have taken jailed accused Avinash Shukla on a 24-hour remand. Investigators had earlier recovered a Ram Mandir donation chest, ₹20 lakh in cash, more than 1,000 US dollars and jewellery from his house. Police allege that Shukla was involved in counting temple donations. Separately, the administration has begun preparations to demolish the newly built houses of the accused in the alleged donation theft case. The Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) has identified properties that either lack approved building plans or were constructed in violation of regulations. Bulldozer action on properties of accused likely According to sources, the government is preparing strict action against those accused in the donation theft case. The administration has begun preparations for bulldozer action on properties linked to the accused. The Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) has identified houses where construction violates rules or where building maps were not approved. Properties under scrutiny include houses built by the accused after joining temple-related work. These include the under-construction house of accused Lavkush Mishra in Shahadatganj and Anukalp Mishra’s house in Kaushalpuri, which may face demolition. ADA is likely to issue notices to them soon. A video has also surfaced showing accused Avinash Shukla’s brother Amit Shukla holding bundles of cash, which is currently under police investigation. Further questioning of trust members likely After questioning accused Avinash Shukla in Ayodhya jail on June 30, police are continuing their investigation. Earlier, Ram Temple Trust general secretary Champat Rai was questioned for nearly three hours on Sunday. Now, Anil Mishra may also be questioned for cross-verification, particularly regarding the appointment of accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The case first came to light on June 7. The Uttar Pradesh government formed an SIT on June 13. An FIR was registered on June 25, and eight accused, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested. On the same day, Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr. Anil Mishra also resigned.

stories.title: Mother, daughter among 3 killed as Scorpio crashes into truck:People were returning from Haridwar; 4 others critically injured
stories.summary: A high-speed Scorpio rammed into a truck from behind on Thursday morning around 7 am in Ayodhya. Three people travelling in the vehicle died in the accident, while four others are critically injured. The impact was so severe that the vehicle’s roof was ripped off and the front portion was completely crushed. The wheels of the Scorpio came off and were thrown out of the vehicle. Seven people were inside at the time of the crash. Three of them died on the spot after getting trapped inside the mangled car. Locals rushed to the scene after hearing screams and immediately informed the police and ambulance services. Police and emergency teams later arrived at the spot and rescued the trapped passengers by breaking the vehicle’s windshield. The injured were taken to the district hospital by ambulance, where they are currently receiving treatment. The accident took place on the Ayodhya-Lucknow National Highway near Mubarakganj in the Raunahi police station area, around 35 km from the Ram Mandir, at about 7 am. First see three pictures Severe impact: roof ripped off, wheels detached The collision between the truck and the Scorpio was so powerful that the vehicle’s roof was completely torn off. The car was heavily crushed from the front, and its doors were broken apart. The passengers were trapped inside the wreckage due to the impact. One of the wheels broke off and fell at a distance. The entire roof collapsed and separated from the body of the vehicle. Family returning from Haridwar among injured Doctors at Ayodhya District Hospital, including Dr. Pankaj Kumar, said that four injured persons were brought in around 10 am by ambulance. All of them belong to the same family. They were returning to Gonda’s Maskanwa village after visiting Haridwar. The injured have been identified as Vijay Lakshmi, Abhishek Gupta, Radheshyam and Ayush. All are undergoing treatment. Overspeeding suspected, vehicle lost control According to eyewitnesses, the Scorpio was coming from the Lucknow side at a very high speed, reportedly over 100 km/h. As it reached Mubarakganj on the Ayodhya-Lucknow highway, it approached a truck ahead of it. Due to excessive speed, the driver lost control and the vehicle rammed into the rear of the truck. The Scorpio partially went under the truck, creating a loud explosion-like sound. Parts of the vehicle were scattered across the road, and bloodstains were visible at several spots. High alert on highway, traffic jam after accident Following the crash, traffic on the highway came to a standstill. Police were informed immediately and reached the spot along with ambulances. A crane was also called to the scene. Rescue teams broke the vehicle’s windshield to pull out the trapped passengers. After shifting the injured to hospital, both vehicles were removed using cranes, and traffic movement was restored. Identities of deceased not confirmed yet Raunahi police station in-charge Ratan Sharma confirmed that three people died in the collision between the truck and Scorpio. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Four injured persons are undergoing treatment at the hospital. The exact cause of the accident is still under investigation, officials said.

stories.title: UP TET exam begins amid tight security:Women asked to remove bangles, anklets; 20 lakh candidates to appear in 3 days
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (UP-TET) 2026 began on Thursday, marking the first day of the three-day examination scheduled till July 4. Candidates were allowed entry at examination centres between 7.15 am and 8.45 am after multiple layers of verification, including admit card checks, biometric matching and retina scanning. The first shift is being conducted from 9.30 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will run from 2.30 pm to 5 pm. Strict security checks across centres In Gorakhpur, female candidates were required to remove bangles, anklets, hairpins and gold chains before entry. Male candidates were asked to leave scarves, caps and belts outside, while shirt sleeves were unfolded for inspection. In Hathras, girls were asked to open their hair buns for checking, while in Prayagraj, candidates had to remove shoes and socks during frisking. In Deoria, 330 police personnel are also appearing for the examination, having taken official leave for the same. The examination is being conducted across 955 centres in 60 districts over three days. A total of 19.94 lakh candidates are appearing, including 17,67,180 from Uttar Pradesh and 2,27,481 from other states. Around 1,85,791 in-service teachers are also part of the examination. Anti-cheating measures and security arrangements The examination authorities have implemented strict measures to ensure a fair and transparent process. Intelligence agencies have been placed on alert, while question paper boxes have been colour-coded and fitted with one-time digital locks. These will be opened 45 minutes before the exam begins to prevent any possibility of leakage. The examination materials are sealed in tamper-proof containers, and different sets of question papers will be decided just five hours before the exam. CCTV feeds from all centres are being monitored live from a control room in Lucknow, while district-level control rooms have also been set up. Biometric verification and iris scanning are mandatory at entry points to prevent impersonation. The entire verification process has been designed to be completed within one minute per candidate. Guidelines and restrictions Candidates have been advised to reach centres at least 60 minutes before the exam. Mobile phones, smart watches, earphones and all electronic devices are strictly prohibited. Any violation of OMR sheet rules, including incorrect marking or multiple responses, will lead to disqualification. On ground reports from districts In Bareilly, candidates were seen interacting with officials before entry into centres. In Hathras, female candidates were checked after opening their hair buns, while in Gorakhpur, strict frisking included removal of jewellery and accessories. In Deoria, biometric machines arrived late at one centre, causing delays and queues. Around 303 police personnel are also appearing for the exam in the district. In Prayagraj, candidates underwent detailed frisking, including removal of footwear and socks. In Ayodhya, 17 centres are hosting 37,920 candidates under tight security arrangements with CCTV surveillance and deployment of magistrates and police personnel. In Kanpur, nearly 70,000 candidates are appearing across 32 centres over three days, with strict multi-layered checks before entry. Government and administrative measures Prayagraj DM Manish Kumar Verma confirmed adequate police deployment and monitoring of candidates arriving from outside the state. Social media surveillance is also being carried out to prevent misinformation. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed strict action against any attempt of cheating or paper leaks, with intelligence units and cyber teams placed on alert across the state. Why many teachers are appearing for TET Around 1.86 lakh in-service teachers who have not cleared TET are also appearing for the exam. Following a recent Supreme Court directive, clearing TET has been made mandatory for teachers teaching up to Class 8 by August 31, 2027, failing which they may face job implications. Promotion opportunities have also been impacted for those without the qualification. Exam design and paper security OMR sheets and question papers are stored in sealed trunks with one-time locks, opened only 45 minutes before the exam using wire cutters. The selection of question paper sets will be finalised just hours before the exam to ensure security. Invigilators are being assigned through randomisation 30 minutes before the exam to ensure transparency and prevent manipulation.

stories.title: Rain in 20 UP districts as monsoon reaches Lucknow:Thunderstorm alert issued across all 75 districts amid changing weather patterns
stories.summary: In Ayodhya, cloudy conditions were reported with local reporters providing continuous updates. In Barabanki, the weather changed suddenly and heavy rain began around 7 am, disrupting normal activity. In Ballia, continuous rainfall since early morning damaged parwal crops, with farmers fearing significant losses if the situation continues. In Sikanderpur area, a lightning strike killed farmer Premchand Yadav while he was working in the fields. Rampur witnessed heavy rain from the early hours, accompanied by strong winds, marking a sharp change in weather conditions. In Kanpur, dense clouds covered the sky with intermittent drizzle throughout the morning. Although wind remained calm and humidity stayed high, rainfall is expected later in the day. Meerut also remained under cloudy skies since morning, with temperatures dropping by nearly 10 degrees following the previous day’s rain. The possibility of further rainfall remains high. Rain alerts and warnings The Meteorological Department has issued heavy rainfall alerts for 24 districts, including Banda, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra, Meerut, Rampur and Bareilly. An orange alert has also been issued for thunderstorms and lightning in 28 districts, including Banda, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi. Flooded streets and rain damage In Mirzapur, nearly two hours of rainfall led to waterlogging in an underpass along the Varanasi–Mirzapur road. In Azamgarh, several roads were submerged under knee-deep water, leaving vehicles stranded. In Lalitpur, heavy rain caused flooding in the GRP police station and nearby areas. Weather conditions (2nd July, 2026 – Morning) In Varanasi, light cloud cover was observed with wind speeds of around 10 km/h. The temperature was recorded at 30°C with humidity at 84%, and rainfall is expected in the coming days. In Saharanpur, cloudy skies persisted since morning, with a rain alert issued till July 7, which is expected to bring a drop in temperatures. Monsoon forecast and rainfall outlook Weather experts have warned that rainfall in Uttar Pradesh this monsoon season may remain around 8% below normal. The expected rainfall is projected between 754 mm and 773 mm, compared to the average of 820 mm to 840 mm. Why rainfall may be lower this year Meteorologists say weakening La Niña conditions and a shift towards El Niño may reduce rainfall activity this year. Reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere earlier in the year is also expected to impact monsoon strength. In contrast, Uttar Pradesh recorded 10–15% above-normal rainfall during last year’s monsoon season.

stories.title: Lucknow fire-linked illegal building to be demolished after 7th July:LDA to recover expenses from plot owner; no response to notice received
stories.summary: A building in Aliganj Sector-D in Lucknow is now likely to face demolition as the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) prepares for bulldozer action over alleged illegal construction. The LDA had issued a notice to the landowner on June 23, asking them to explain within 15 days why the construction was carried out without approval. Officials said no response has been received so far from the owner. With the notice period ending on July 6, demolition action is expected to begin on July 7. LDA officials said the entire cost of demolition will also be recovered from the property owner. Preparations for the action are in the final stage, and police support will be taken to maintain law and order during the drive. SIT report flags Electricity Department role in fire case Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing a fire incident has nearly completed its investigation and submitted its report to the government. According to sources, the findings not only point to lapses by LDA engineers but also raise serious questions about the functioning of the electricity department. The report states that the building was given an electricity connection in violation of rules. It also notes that even after increased electricity load, no effective action was taken by the department, leading to continued safety violations. Statements of suspended engineers recorded During the investigation, the SIT also recorded statements of LDA engineers who were suspended following the fire incident. The report is now under review at the government level, after which further action against officials and departments will be decided.

stories.title: Woman films reel on SP's chair:Spins around in seat; deletes Instagram account, apologises after action
stories.summary: A reel shot by the daughter-in-law of a retired police sub-inspector inside the SP office auditorium in Auraiya has triggered controversy. The video was recorded at around 2 pm on June 30 and surfaced at around 4.30 pm on Wednesday after she uploaded it on Instagram, from where it was widely shared. The video shows the woman sitting on the SP's chair and spinning around in it. After the clip went viral, SP Abhishek Bharti ordered action. The woman and her father-in-law later apologised, and she deleted her Instagram account. Family members attended retirement ceremony A farewell function for retired police personnel was held at the SP office on Tuesday. Dibiyapur sub-inspector Nem Singh was among those retiring, and members of his family had attended the programme. After the event concluded and the auditorium was vacated, Nem Singh's daughter-in-law, Soni Chaudhary, sat on the chair and recorded a reel. She later uploaded it on Instagram. The video went viral on Wednesday, causing a stir within the police department. After being informed about the viral reel, SP Abhishek Bharti directed immediate action. Retired officer Nem Singh and his daughter-in-law admitted their mistake and apologised. Soni Chaudhary also released a video apologising for the incident. Daughter-in-law had 16000 followers on Instagram Police let her off after issuing a warning and asking her not to repeat such an act in the future. Soni later deleted her Instagram account, which reportedly had around 16,000 followers. SP Abhishek Bharti said the reel had been recorded after the auditorium became empty. Since she apologised and assured police that she would not repeat the act, no further action was taken. Father-in-law said - I have got the reel deleted Nem Singh said a programme had been organised in the SP office conference hall to mark the retirement of police personnel and that members of his family had attended. He said his daughter-in-law recorded the reel after the event ended and that he had it deleted immediately after learning about it. Daughter-in-law apologized with folded hands, said - A mistake was made Soni Chaudhary said she had attended her father-in-law's retirement ceremony and made the reel while sitting on a chair kept inside the conference room after the programme ended. She said she later realised her mistake and deleted the reel immediately at her father-in-law's insistence. "Such a mistake will not happen again. I should not have done this. I sincerely apologise for my actions. It was a very big mistake on my part," she said.
