stories.title: Man burnt alive while sleeping in Baghpat:Family claims wife her lover set him on fire
stories.summary: In Baghpat, a man succumbed to his injuries a week after he was allegedly set on fire by his wife and her lover. According to reports, the incident took place on June 20 in the Binauli police station area, around 38 kilometres from the district headquarters. While the victim was asleep at night, his wife allegedly poured petrol on him, which she had obtained through her lover, and set him ablaze. Engulfed in flames, the young man ran out of the house screaming for help. Hearing his cries, locals rushed to the spot and managed to douse the fire before shifting him to the Community Health Centre (CHC) in critical condition. He was later referred to Meerut District Hospital due to the severity of his injuries. Despite undergoing treatment for a week, he died on Friday night. Before his death, he reportedly told police that his wife and her lover were responsible for the attack. Police have since arrested both accused and sent them to jail. See 3 pictures related to the incident... Now know the complete matter. Rajiv (40) was a resident of Bijwara village. In the family are wife Neeshu (37), daughter Pari (9), son Kallu (7), Shiva (4) and father Satbir Singh (62). He used to support the family by doing labor work. According to family members, Neeshu had been having an affair with neighbor Vikrant (40) for 5 years. Three months ago, Rajiv came to know about this. He forbade both of them from meeting, but both did not agree. It is alleged that during this time both of them conspired to remove Rajiv from the way. On the evening of June 20, Rajiv returned home from work. He ate food with his wife and went to sleep in the room at 11 pm. Wife Neeshu went to another room with the children. It is alleged that at 1 am when Rajiv was in deep sleep, Neeshu called Vikrant home. He arrived with two liters of petrol. Both went into Rajiv's room and sprinkled petrol on him. Rajiv woke up from sleep due to the petrol and started running out of the room. During this time, Neeshu lit a matchstick and set him on fire. Father saw lover fleeing Rajiv's father Satbir Singh said that after the incident, he saw Vikrant fleeing from the house. He filed an FIR against both of them at Binauli police station on June 21. According to the father, the daughter-in-law had called her lover home and both together poured petrol on the sleeping Rajiv and set him on fire. After this, the accused lover Vikrant fled through the roof. They also alleged that before the incident, Vikrant had threatened to kill Rajiv. After recording Rajiv's statement, the police arrested Neeshu and Vikrant on June 22 and sent them to jail. Death occurred during treatment Rajiv was undergoing treatment at Meerut District Hospital. After battling between life and death for six days, he died late Friday night. Following this, the police added murder charges against both the accused. Wife and lover were arrested - Inspector Inspector Binauli Rakesh Kumar Sharma stated- Action has already been taken in the case. After the injured person's statement, his wife and her lover were arrested. After the death of the injured Rajeev, now murder charges will be added against both of them.

stories.title: Varanasi 8th hottest city in India:41°C temperature recorded; June rainfall remains low at 10%
stories.summary: The severe heatwave continues to grip Purvanchal, with temperatures rising to 40.5°C by Saturday afternoon. Wind speeds of around 8 km/h and humidity levels of 53% were recorded in the region. Meteorologists have predicted that a mild monsoon influence may reach the district within the next 48 hours, which could bring much-needed relief from the intense heat. See 2 pictures BHU's special preparations before monsoon To deal with the problem of potential heavy rainfall and waterlogging, BHU administration has started comprehensive preparations. Powerful pumps are being installed for rainwater drainage in low-lying areas including Sunderlal Hospital, Trauma Center, hostels and residential complexes. With the help of these pumps, rainwater will be quickly drained out so that waterlogging situations do not occur in hospitals and other important complexes. BHU has prepared an action plan in collaboration with Municipal Corporation The university administration has prepared a coordinated action plan in collaboration with the Municipal Corporation and Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam. Under the campaign running since June 6th, work is being carried out at a rapid pace to clean the rainwater drainage network, remove silt from drains, and strengthen the drainage system. The university's construction department, sanitation and support services, and horticulture department are jointly engaged in cleaning all major drains before the monsoon. Within the next two to three days, pumps will be installed in trauma centers and other sensitive areas. Agriculture Department's advice to farmers: cultivate coarse grains In view of the lack of rainfall, District Agriculture Officer Birendra Kumar has advised farmers to remain alert. He informed that this year, due to the effect of El Nio, there has been less than normal rainfall in the month of June and the possibility of good rain ahead also appears low. He said that in areas where there is no adequate irrigation arrangement, farmers should give priority to the cultivation of pulses and millets (coarse grains). Farmers who have irrigation facilities available have been advised to transplant paddy varieties that mature in 100 to 110 days, so that the impact of potential drought is minimized. The Agriculture Department has also appealed to farmers to definitely get crop insurance. Electricity demand at record level The impact of severe heat is clearly visible on electricity consumption as well. In the district, demand for more than 900 megawatts of electricity has been continuously recorded for the past ten days. On June 25, the highest demand of 970 megawatts of electricity was recorded in the district. Electricity demand in the four districts of Varanasi division - Varanasi, Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur - continues to remain at high levels. Due to increasing consumption, pressure on the electricity system has increased.

stories.title: UPTET-2026 to be held in Varanasi:Admit cards to be issued from 30 June; exam scheduled from 2 to 4 July
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has completed all preparations for UPTET-2026. Under the supervision of Commission Chairman Dr. Prashant Kumar, the examination will be conducted with complete transparency and impartiality across 955 centres in 60 districts of the state, including Varanasi. UPTET-2026 will be held from July 2 to 4 in multiple shifts. On July 2, the Upper Primary Level (Classes 6 to 8) examination will be conducted in both shifts. On July 3, the Upper Primary Level exam will take place in the first shift, while the Primary Level (Classes 1 to 5) exam will be held in the second shift. On July 4, the Primary Level examination will be conducted in the first shift only. The first shift will run from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM, while the second shift will be from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM. The Commission has uploaded detailed information regarding examination districts on its official website https://upessc.up.gov.in from June 22. Candidates can verify their details through the link provided on the website and check their allotted examination district. Admit cards will be available for download from June 30 on the Commission’s website. The Chairman has advised candidates to download their admit cards on time and strictly follow the instructions mentioned. No candidate will be allowed entry to the examination centre without a valid admit card.

stories.title: Mukesh Khanna lashes out on Ram Mandir donation scam:Actor says 'They are worse than thieves, they are robbing God'
stories.summary: Senior actor Mukesh Khanna has lashed out at the donation scam that occurred at the Ram Temple. He says that those who steal in the temple are above thieves, dacoits, or any dishonest person. He has appealed that devotees should stop offering donations to the temple. Mukesh Khanna wrote from his official Instagram account, Do you know, your cash offerings in temples do not reach God. It gets lost somewhere in between. There is widespread looting. There's a saying, 'Loot if you can.' And those who loot are abundant here. I once said, 'Thieves, dacoits, and dishonest people are abundant, yet my country is great.' But what name should I give to these donation looters? Thieves, dacoits, or dishonest people? None of these. Because they are above all of them. They are not only looting devotees but also God.' Further, he wrote, 'I would only advise devotees that if there's no bamboo, there's no flute (meaning, remove the root cause), similarly, if there's no offering, there's no scam. So stop making offerings. Especially money and jewellery. God will be pleased.' What is the whole matter? On June 7, a case of theft of offerings at the Ram Temple came to light. An SIT was formed to investigate the theft of offerings on the orders of the Yogi government. Initial investigations indicated irregularities in matters related to donations, offerings, and management. Based on the SIT report, the police registered an FIR against 8 named accused, arrested and sent them to jail. This made the whole matter serious. Meanwhile, Champat Rai, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Trust, and Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra have resigned. According to sources, Gopal Rao, in charge of temple construction, has also been removed from the temple's management.

stories.title: Yogi says, 'BJP secured Indian borders':UP CM claims before 2014 enemies threatened India; now air and surgical strikes follow
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the BJP Mahanagar's two-day training camp on Saturday. Addressing party workers, he said India's approach to national security has changed significantly since 2014. Yogi said that before 2014, Indian soldiers were subjected to atrocities by enemy countries, but governments hesitated to respond for fear of harming diplomatic relations. "There was a time when relations with other countries were prioritized over national interest. But after 2014, India has shown the capability to look the enemy in the eye. If anyone encroaches on our borders or attacks Indian soldiers, no one can stop us from carrying out air strikes or surgical strikes," he said. He added that the BJP has demonstrated its resolve and capability in securing India's borders before both the country and the world. See pictures… The Chief Minister said Naxalism is now confined to just one or two districts and will soon be eliminated. He also claimed that terrorism in Kashmir and insurgency in the Northeast have been brought to an end. "Development is possible only when there is security. A strong infrastructure accelerates the country's growth," he said.

stories.summary: Dhirendra Shastri turned emotional over the theft at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. He said, "Ravan still exists—only his form has changed. Ravan had only abducted Mata Janaki, but this theft has robbed the faith and trust of lakhs and crores of devotees." 'God will also punish the accused' Shastri said an FIR has been registered and demanded a thorough investigation. "The truth is the truth, whether people like it or not. Those who stole the offerings will face government punishment, and God will also give them the greatest punishment," he said. Accused spend restless first night in jail According to jail sources, Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu and the seven other accused spent a sleepless first night in Faizabad Jail. They were reportedly discussing the case among themselves and arguing with each other. All eight accused will be produced in court again on Monday.

stories.title: 2 children die in Lucknow Muharram procession:Balcony collapses during refreshment distribution; 8 trapped under debris
stories.summary: During a Muharram procession in Lucknow, two 12-year-old boys died after the balcony of a house collapsed. Eight people, including four children, were trapped under the debris. Police rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared Ali (12) and Arman (12) dead. After initial treatment, the injured were referred to the KGMU Trauma Centre and a 100-bed hospital. According to police, the incident occurred around 10:15 PM on June 26 in the Pakhariya locality of Mohana, under the Itaunja police station area. A Muharram procession was passing through the locality when members of a family, seated on a six-foot-high balcony outside their house, were distributing sharbat to participants. The balcony suddenly gave way, triggering panic as around 10 people were buried under the debris. People in the procession immediately alerted the police and began rescue efforts by removing the rubble. Police and emergency teams soon reached the spot, and the injured were taken to hospital by ambulance. After the situation was brought under control, the Muharram procession was allowed to continue. 3 pictures Now understand entire matter- According to police, Mushtaq (40), who lives in Pakhariya locality, was standing on his house's balcony and distributing sharbat to people participating in the Muharram procession along with his family. In the rush to get sharbat, several people hung from the balcony. Due to this, the balcony collapsed. Many people got trapped underneath it. In the accident, Ali (12) son of Qasim and Arman (12) son of Imran, who were standing below, died. Ajmal (7) son of Zakki, Ziyan (3), Sana (30) wife of Sharif, Mohammad Haseeb (42) son of Safiq and Ziaul (30) son of Hamid were seriously injured. The condition of Rusida daughter of Liyaqat remains critical. Daud (12) and Abdul Wajood (10) son of Shadab were discharged after first aid. It was fortunate that the family standing on top of the balcony received only minor injuries in the accident. Otherwise, the accident could have been much worse. 'My brother-in-law was also injured' Abrar said - Sherbet was being distributed. The crowd had increased. During this, the canopy collapsed. Many people were injured. Among them, my brother-in-law Haseeb was also seriously injured. His treatment is ongoing. Sumaiya said, “I had gone to get sherbet for the children. During this time the canopy fell. My son Jiyan and husband Haseeb were seriously injured.” DCP North Gopal Chaudhary said- 2 children have died due to the collapse of a canopy. 8 people are injured. Treatment of the injured is ongoing.

stories.title: Monsoon likely in two days:Rain, thunderstorm alert in 30 UP districts, temperatures to drop by 8°C
stories.summary: Monsoon continues to elude Uttar Pradesh, with its arrival delayed by nearly two weeks. The southwest monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj on the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar border for the past 15 days. It usually enters the state by June 20, but this year it is now expected to arrive around June 29, nearly eight days behind schedule. Most parts of the state woke up to bright sunshine on Saturday morning. Mild winds kept temperatures slightly lower in the early hours, but the heat is expected to intensify through the day. Several cities are likely to record temperatures above 42°C, while hot winds will add to people's discomfort. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for 30 districts, with lightning expected at isolated places. A heatwave warning remains in place for 22 districts. On Friday, Lakhimpur Kheri was the hottest city in the state at 43.2°C, followed by Banda and Agra (43°C each), Lucknow (42.4°C), Aligarh (42.2°C) and Prayagraj (42°C). The weather department said monsoon showers are likely to begin in Uttar Pradesh within the next two days. Even areas that do not receive rain immediately are expected to witness increased cloud cover. Temperatures are likely to fall by 8–9°C, bringing relief from the scorching heat and heatwave conditions. Widespread rainfall is expected across most parts of the state from June 30. 'Conditions favourable for monsoon to enter UP in two days' Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said, "The southwest monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj for the past 15 days. Conditions are now becoming favourable for its advance into Uttar Pradesh over the next two days. Heatwave conditions will continue in parts of the state today and tomorrow. However, eastern Uttar Pradesh, the Terai region and a few other areas may witness strong winds and light rainfall during this period." Weather forecast for the next five days Rainfall remains uneven across Uttar Pradesh Rainfall has been uneven across the state's 75 districts this June. Thirty-four districts have recorded a large rainfall deficit, while 13 have received below-normal rain. Sixteen districts have reported normal rainfall, four have recorded above-normal rainfall and seven have received significantly more rainfall than usual. Kaushambi has not recorded any rainfall so far this month. Why is the monsoon moving slowly? According to the weather department, the weakening of the jet stream is delaying the advance of the southwest monsoon. Meteorologists expect it to move forward once atmospheric conditions improve. UP may receive 8% below-normal rainfall this season Senior scientist Atul Singh said Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive below-normal rainfall this monsoon season. The state usually records 820–840 mm of rainfall between June and September, but this year it is expected to receive only 754–773 mm, around 8% below normal. El Niño signals raise concern IMD Director General Dr M. Mahapatra said La Niña-like conditions over the Pacific Ocean are fading and signs of El Niño are emerging, which could reduce rainfall this year. Reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere during January–March may also affect the strength of the southwest monsoon. Impact on farming and food prices Below-normal rainfall could affect Uttar Pradesh's economy, agriculture and daily life. Paddy production may decline by up to 20%, while delayed rainfall in June and July could postpone paddy transplantation and reduce the cultivated area. Farmers may have to rely more on tube wells for irrigation, increasing electricity and diesel costs. Lower crop production could push up the prices of cereals, pulses and vegetables. Drought conditions may also deepen in Bundelkhand and parts of south-western Uttar Pradesh, including Jhansi, Mahoba, Lalitpur and Mathura. Last year's monsoon was above normal According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh received an average of 870–900 mm of rainfall during the 2025 monsoon season (June to September), around 10–15% above the long-term average.

stories.title: Eyewitnesses blame delayed fire brigade response in Lucknow blaze:Claim 15 deaths could have been prevented; Bhaskar conducts reality check
stories.summary: Smoke was coming out from parts of the building. We realised people were trapped inside. We broke the windows by throwing stones, and 4-5 people managed to come down. If the fire brigade had arrived on time, around 15 people could have been saved. The fire brigade did not arrive half an hour late, but after nearly an hour. Even if it had reached within 15-20 minutes, the lives of 15 children could have been saved. These allegations were made by eyewitnesses and families of the victims in the Lucknow fire tragedy. Following these claims, a Bhaskar reporter conducted a reality check. The distance between the accident site and the nearest fire station was covered on a scooter at around 3 pm, the same time the fire broke out. According to official records, the fire station received information at 2:27 pm, while the FIR registered at Aliganj police station states that the fire started at 2:30 pm. This report examines the eyewitness accounts, the route between Kapurthala and Indiranagar Fire Station, and the situation at the accident site. Now see the condition of the building- What happened in the fire? A massive fire broke out on June 22 in a two-storey building in Lucknow's Aliganj area after an alleged AC blast. Five people managed to escape by climbing down through pipes and electrical wires. One youth jumped from the building to save himself but suffered paralysis in both legs. The blaze claimed the lives of 15 students who were attending classes at a 3D animation centre on the second floor. On June 23, an SIT and forensic team inspected the building and questioned the injured at KGMU Hospital. After post-mortem examinations, the bodies were handed over to their families. Following the incident, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) ordered the demolition of the building. Reality check: Reporter reached fire station in 20 minutes The nearest fire station to the accident site is Indiranagar Fire Station, about 6.2 km away. Google Maps estimates the journey by car at 18 minutes. To verify the route, the reporter travelled the same distance on a scooter at around 3 pm and reached the fire station in 20 minutes. However, fire engines move differently from two-wheelers. Officials said 19 fire vehicles, including a hydraulic rescue unit, were sent from different fire stations to tackle the blaze. Eyewitnesses speak 'People broke the windows to rescue those trapped' Eyewitness Sahil Joshi said he was passing by on his bike when he saw smoke rising from the building. People started throwing stones to break the windows. Three to four boys climbed down using electrical wires. Many others remained trapped inside. The entire incident lasted around 20-25 minutes. Everyone kept calling the police and fire brigade, but the fire brigade arrived late. 'Fire trucks reached after more than half an hour' Local resident Kamini said she rushed outside after hearing screams. There was panic everywhere. People were breaking the windows with bricks so the smoke could escape. As soon as the glass shattered, some people tried to jump from the building. We wanted to help but could not. The fire trucks also arrived late, more than half an hour after the fire started. 'The fire engine reached after nearly an hour' Renu, sister-in-law of deceased Neelesh, blamed the delay in the fire brigade's arrival for the high death toll. The fire engine did not arrive after half an hour—it came nearly an hour later. If it had reached even 10-20 minutes earlier, many children could have survived. We lost Neelesh because help did not arrive on time. 'The fire brigade always reaches late' Shubham Mishra, who visited the site, claimed delays were common. The biggest negligence is that the fire brigade always reaches late. Two months ago, my shop caught fire and the fire brigade arrived only after everything had burned. Like police vehicles are stationed at major intersections, fire engines should also be kept ready at key locations so they can respond immediately during emergencies.

stories.title: Lucknow property dealer murder case:Accused killed after being cornered in STF encounter
stories.summary: The main shooter in the murder of Lucknow property dealer Sandeep Singh was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) early on Saturday. Police said the accused, Sanjay alias Sanjeev, opened fire with a carbine after the STF surrounded him on Indira Canal Road. The STF retaliated, killing him in the exchange of fire. Sanjeev had been carrying a reward of ₹1 lakh since the murder of Sandeep Singh on May 27. The property dealer was shot dead outside his office in broad daylight while he was talking on his mobile phone. Two bike-borne attackers opened fire on him and fled. Dainik Bhaskar had accessed the exclusive CCTV footage of the incident. How the murder took place On May 27, between 12 pm and 12:30 pm, Sandeep Singh (42) arrived at his office in the PGI police station area with his driver, Pradeep Singh. As he stepped out of his car and walked towards the office, two masked men arrived on a motorcycle. One of the attackers, dressed in a white shirt and blue jeans, ran towards Sandeep and opened fire. The first bullet hit him in the chest, causing him to collapse on the road. The attacker continued firing even after Sandeep fell and finally shot him near the head. The second accused waited on a running Apache motorcycle. After the shooting, the gunman ran back, got on the bike, and both escaped. The rider was wearing a helmet, while the shooter had covered his face with a white cloth. People nearby rushed Sandeep to Apex Trauma Centre, where he died during treatment. Police recovered a 50-second CCTV recording of the attack. CCTV captures the attack Property dealer was from Jaunpur Sandeep Singh was a native of Takari village in Jaunpur district. He lived with his family near Kalindi Park in Vrindavan Yojana, Lucknow. He is survived by his wife, Preeti Singh, an 11-year-old son, Sarthak, and a nine-year-old daughter, CV Singh. His elder brother, Satish Singh, lives in their native village. Sandeep moved to Lucknow in 2008 to live with his uncle, Rajendra Prasad Singh, a government inter college principal. He later entered the real estate business and, around one-and-a-half years ago, opened an office under the name PSS Builders Private Limited in Yadav Complex, Kalli Paschim Bazaar.

stories.title: RSS pressure before Champat Rai's resignation:Haridwar meeting triggered scrutiny, sources say he was told to step down
stories.summary: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned from their posts on Friday amid growing pressure over the alleged Ram Mandir donation theft case. Sources said the developments were set in motion after a Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) meeting held in Haridwar on June 18 and 19. Champat Rai and Gopal Rao from Ayodhya attended the meeting. According to sources, RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale questioned both leaders over allegations related to Ram Mandir donations and sought an explanation regarding alleged irregularities in donation accounts. After the meeting, pressure on Champat Rai reportedly increased, and senior Sangh leaders began distancing themselves from him. Champat Rai kept away during CM Yogi's Ayodhya visit: Sources Sources claimed that during Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's Ayodhya visit on June 19, Champat Rai was kept away from the Chief Minister's official programmes. With pressure continuing to mount, Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra submitted their resignations to Trust president Mahant Nritya Gopal Das on Friday. RSS and VHP leaders reportedly advised him to step down Sources said Champat Rai received calls from RSS and VHP leaders throughout Thursday night. Some leaders reportedly advised him to resign to help contain the controversy. On Friday morning, Champat Rai performed prayers before reaching Mani Ramdas Ji's camp. Dr Anil Mishra was also called there. Around 11 am, both leaders submitted their resignations to the Trust president. FIR filed 18 days after donation theft came to light The alleged theft of offerings at Ram Mandir came to light on June 7. Eighteen days later, police registered an FIR against eight people linked to the Trust. The FIR did not name some of the Trust's prominent office-bearers, triggering criticism on social media. Opposition leaders alleged that senior functionaries had been protected. Five reasons behind the resignations Questions raised during the SIT's preliminary probe The Special Investigation Team (SIT), formed to investigate the alleged theft of offerings, reportedly found indications of irregularities in matters related to donations, offerings and temple management. Sources said Champat Rai's role also came under scrutiny. FIR and arrests increased the pressure Based on the SIT's findings, police registered an FIR against eight accused and later arrested them. The arrests intensified the controversy and increased pressure on the Trust. Former driver's name surfaced in the FIR The FIR names Champat Rai's former driver Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu and his nephew Manish. Investigators allege they manipulated temple offerings along with others associated with the temple, making the case more sensitive. Trust wanted an independent investigation According to sources, the Trust believed senior office-bearers stepping down would prevent questions over the fairness of the investigation and allow agencies to carry out the probe independently. Move aimed at protecting the Trust's credibility Sources said the Trust decided that resignations were necessary to ensure the ongoing investigation did not affect the credibility of Ram Mandir, which is visited by millions of devotees. Saints demanded a wider probe into temple-related bodies During the VHP meeting in Haridwar, several saints reportedly demanded that the investigation should not be limited to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. They also called for a probe into the accounts and expenditure of the Ramalaya Trust, founded by late Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati, and the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Construction Committee, which handled temple construction work before the Supreme Court's verdict in the Ram Janmabhoomi case. VHP postponed Ayodhya meeting amid growing controversy Amid growing anger among saints over the alleged theft of offerings, the VHP postponed its four-day Central Managing Committee meeting scheduled to begin in Ayodhya on June 26. The meeting was to be held at Karsevakpuram, with representatives from all 44 VHP provinces expected to attend. Trust issued clarification on Kagbhushundi idol and silver bricks The controversy widened after allegations surfaced that a donated Kagbhushundi idol and silver bricks had gone missing. On June 24, Akhilesh Yadav claimed on social media that the donated Kagbhushundi idol had disappeared and questioned repeated reports of theft involving temple donations. On Friday, Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut questioned the whereabouts of four kilograms of silver donated by Uddhav Thackeray for Ram Mandir and demanded accountability. The Trust later released photographs stating that the Kagbhushundi idol is kept safely at Karsevakpuram, while the silver bricks remain secure in bank lockers. VHP opposes dissolving the Ram Mandir Trust VHP International Working President Alok Kumar said there is no need to dissolve the Ram Mandir Trust or constitute a new committee. He said the allegations are against certain individuals and not against the Trust as an institution. 'Focus should be on transparency and better management' Alok Kumar said the priority should be to strengthen the temple's management through modern technology, improved monitoring systems and greater transparency. Responding to questions over the SIT investigation, he said the FIR names eight accused but also refers to "others", indicating that the investigation will not be limited to those already named. He said all those found responsible would face a fair and comprehensive investigation.

stories.title: Pooja Pal takes over as BJP state vice president:Party's membership rules come under spotlight; what SP's 7 rebels got?
stories.summary: The BJP's appointment of MLA Pooja Pal as its Uttar Pradesh vice-president has triggered questions over whether the party relaxed its own organisational rules. Expelled from the SP on 14 August, 2025, Pooja was elevated to the key post just 10 months and 12 days later, even though no public record or photograph of her formally joining the BJP has surfaced. According to the BJP constitution, only an 'active member' can hold an organisational post. To qualify as an active member, a person must enroll at least 100 general members. Despite this requirement, Pooja Pal was directly appointed to the state organization. Pooja Pal is currently an attached MLA in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, meaning she is technically an independent legislator. When asked by Dainik Bhaskar whether she had joined the BJP, she replied, ‘I have become a member of the BJP,’ but did not clarify when or where she took the party's membership. Pooja's 'parachute entry' into BJP organisation Becoming a BJP state office-bearer typically requires years of grassroots work through the party's Mandal, district and regional units. One example is Neeraj Singh, son of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who worked for over a decade in the BJP organisation in Lucknow before being appointed State Vice President. In contrast, Pooja Pal was made State Vice President less than 11 months after her expulsion from the SP. Sources said she was also being considered for a ministerial berth during the Yogi government's Cabinet expansion, but the BJP's national leadership ultimately decided against it. No precise answer on when she took membership We spoke to Kaushambi BJP District President Dharamraj Maurya regarding Pooja Pal's membership. He says, Pooja Pal has not become a BJP member from Kaushambi. She must have become a member at the state office level; only the state headquarters can tell about this. In Lucknow, BJP's chief spokesperson Dinesh Pratap Singh says, Pooja Pal is a member of the BJP, which is why she has been made an office bearer. Sometimes photos of joining are released, and sometimes they are not. BJP sending 2 big political messages 1. To make her a face suffering from SP's 'mafia rule' Pooja Pal is the biggest and living example of being a victim of the alleged 'goonda raj' (rule of hooligans) of SP in UP politics. On 25 January, 2005, just 10 days after their marriage, her husband and then-MLA Raju Pal were murdered by the henchmen of Atiq Ahmed. Subsequently, on 24 February, 2023, her maternal cousin Umesh Pal was also publicly murdered. In the assembly elections, BJP will put Pooja Pal forward to remind the public how SP-backed mafias harassed a woman. 2. Focus on UP's 'Pal' vote bank The Pal community has a large vote bank in Uttar Pradesh, which opposition parties have also put all their efforts into wooing. Currently, Shyam Lal Pal is the state president of SP, and Vishwanath Pal is the state president of BSP. To break this encirclement by the opposition, BJP has made these moves- In the Rajya Sabha elections 2024, a total of 7 Samajwadi Party MLAs rebelled by cross-voting. However, not everyone's luck was the same when it came to receiving rewards.

stories.title: Man murders girlfriend after she refuses to elope:Accused arrested in Delhi; friendship started on Instagram
stories.summary: A man allegedly murdered his girlfriend in Amethi after she refused to elope with him. The accused travelled from Pratapgarh on the night of 30 June and called her to a field near her home in Jangal Ramnagar village at around 8.30 pm. During their meeting, he raised the issue of marriage and pressured her to run away with him. When she refused, an argument broke out. Enraged, he allegedly smothered her to death, then covered the body with eucalyptus leaves before fleeing. Police arrested him in Delhi on 3 July and disclosed the case on Saturday afternoon, revealing that the two had become friends through Instagram. Understand the whole case Kajal (19), daughter of Amarjeet Singh, who lives with his family in Jangal Ramnagar village, about 3 km from the Amethi district headquarters, left home at around 7.30 pm on 30 June but did not return. Her family informed the police that night and continued searching for her. On Wednesday morning, villagers found Kajal's body in bushes around 200 metres from her home. Police, along with the CO, ASP and SP, reached the spot and sent the body for post-mortem. Initial investigations indicated it was a murder. Father expressed suspicion on the lover Father Amarjeet Singh filed a case against his daughter's lover, Surjeet Singh. Surjeet is a resident of Udaipur village in the Lalganj police station area of Pratapgarh. Meanwhile, the post-mortem report stated that the girl died due to suffocation. Following this, the police started searching for the accused Surjeet. SP Saravanan T formed 10 teams to unravel the incident. Kajal's mobile was not found at the crime scene. Therefore, the police started tracking Kajal's and Surjeet's mobiles through surveillance. After continuous investigation for 48 hours, the police found Surjeet's location in Delhi. Following this, he was arrested on July 3 from the Kamla Nagar area of Delhi. Misled police, broke down when confronted with location The SP interrogated Surjeet. At first, he denied killing Kajal. Later, when asked about both mobile locations being at the same place, Surjeet broke down. He confessed to the murder. SP Saravanan T said, Kajal and Surjeet had been talking for about two and a half years. Their friendship started on Instagram. On Tuesday night, lover Surjeet reached the village and called Kajal to meet. He pressured Kajal to elope from home for marriage. Pushed her to ground and covered her mouth with both hands Upon Kajal's refusal, he pushed her to the ground. Then, he covered her mouth with both his hands. She died due to suffocation. After this, he broke eucalyptus branches and leaves and placed them over the dead body. Meanwhile, hearing someone approaching, he fled from the scene. While fleeing, he also took Kajal's mobile phone with him. Then, he took a bus from Amethi to Lucknow. From there, he reached Delhi by bus. The police continuously pursued Surjeet. His mobile phone also kept turning on intermittently. Tracking it, the police reached Kamla Nagar in Delhi, where Surjeet was taken into custody and brought to Amethi. SP Sarvanan T said, Kajal's mobile phone has also been recovered from the accused. The police timely solved this case and arrested the accused. The team that worked on the case will be given a reward of 35000 rupees.

stories.title: Doctor allegedly murdered by wife her brother-in-law:Brother says victim married again two months ago
stories.summary: A doctor who had a love marriage two months ago died in hospital at 4 am on Saturday in Bareilly. His brother alleged that the doctor's wife and her brother poisoned him before dumping him outside the Mayor's camp office in the Civil Lines area. Passers-by admitted him to hospital at around 8 pm on Friday. According to the family, the doctor told them before his death that his wife and her brother had brutally assaulted him. They also said his wife had been staying at her brother and sister-in-law's house for the past one and a half months. The incident falls under the Subhash Nagar area. Doctor had love marriage on April 15 Dr Kuldeep Goswami (40), who lived near Balaji Dham Temple in the Subhash Nagar area, ran a private clinic. He had divorced his first wife, Daya, three years ago and had a 13-year-old son, Utkarsh, a Class 7 student at Mother's Public School. Kuldeep married Gunjan (38) in a love marriage on 15 April. According to his brother Vinayak, Gunjan had been pressuring him to live separately from his parents since the wedding and frequently argued with his family members. About 15 days after the marriage, Gunjan left her in-laws' home, allegedly taking jewellery worth lakhs of rupees. She had since been living with her sister and brother-in-law in Sadar Bazaar, under the Cantt police station area. Kuldeep had gone to convince his wife According to the family, Dr Kuldeep had gone to his wife's house on Friday (3 July) to bring her back. They alleged that his wife, along with her sister and brother-in-law, poisoned him. After he died, the accused allegedly dumped his body by the roadside. On Saturday, the deceased's brother lodged a complaint at Cantt police station, accusing the trio of murder. Police have registered a murder case, sent the body for post-mortem, and launched an investigation. What Kuldeep said in the video Kuldeep's video has surfaced. In it, he said, I have become very troubled, that's why I am making this video. My marriage to Gunjan took place two months ago. After marriage I felt that I have been trapped in a well-planned conspiracy.After marriage, cash, gold-silver and other items from my house started disappearing. I once caught Gunjan giving 70 thousand rupees to my sister Reena. When asked, she said she was lending it and would return it later.Gradually, I became convinced that the theft happening in the house was being done by Gunjan herself. When I complained to her family members, they instead became ready to fight and assault. Gunjan's brother Amit had wrong intentions towards our younger sister-in-law. On the 30th, he behaved obscenely with sister-in-law. A complaint was filed at Subhash Nagar police station, but no action was taken.I had great faith in the law, but now I am completely broken. I want an investigation against Gunjan, Reena, Satish, and Amit. They should get the strictest punishment. With folded hands, I request CM Yogi, DM and SSP to conduct an impartial investigation of this entire matter. What happened to me should not happen to anyone else.Utkarsh, son, I love you. Take care of grandfather-grandmother and progress a lot in life. I also request my friends to support my son.

stories.title: 'I'm thinking of stepping down':Kanpur councillor leader's AUDIO emerges; says mayor could have resolved the controversy
stories.summary: We are completely trapped, Vikas... We are thinking of resigning. These unnecessary troubles we are getting, they will stop, Vikas. Those new big leaders of our party (BJP) have come recently, Saurabh Dev, Golu... They don't have to do anything themselves... they are causing us trouble. If we want, we can make everyone sit down and fold their hands today, end the matter, but the Mayor doesn't want to. These things were said by Naveen Pandit, leader of the councillor group, to Vikas Jaiswal, who was opposing the Mayor, after holding a press conference against the rebel councillors in Pramila Auditorium. On Friday, the Dainik Bhaskar App received an audio of the conversation between the two councillors. So, what exactly was discussed for 5 minutes between BJP councillor Naveen Pandit, who held a press conference against the rebel councillors and then on the other hand claimed to be trapped, and rebel councillor Vikas Jaiswal? Read the report Now read the conversation between rebel councillor Vikas Jaiswal and councilor party leader Naveen Pandit Vikas Jaiswal- Where are you? Naveen Pandit- I am at home. Vikas Jaiswal- What happened today, what was the press conference for? Naveen Pandit- Brother, what can I say, I am absolutely... absolutely feeling like this, that it seems to me that in two-three days... what can I say, man, I... Vikas Jaiswal- The matter had just gotten on track with great difficulty. Naveen Pandit- Nothing, these days new big leaders of our party have arrived, Saurabh Dev, Golu. There should be a press conference; they don't want to do anything themselves... Vikas Jaiswal- Saurabh Dev brother, is building houses, bungalows of two hundred square yards each, his wife is working. Golu has earned crores of rupees, have these people come to ruin the BJP or the organisation? Naveen Pandit- They are ruining us. Vikas Jaiswal- Naveen brother, you... I can understand your compulsion. I know how revolutionary you are, I... people were telling us. Naveen Pandit- We are completely trapped, Vikas... Vikas Jaiswal- You told us so many times, let's sit and sort this out... but what to say, we said these people are using Bunty. Naveen Pandit- You understand, they should understand, man, they don't seem to understand. Vikas Jaiswal- They are steeped in arrogance. Naveen Pandit- What to say, they... let's finish the talk, it bothers me, they are family members, it's a family, still nothing. If we want today, we can make everyone sit down and fold their hands, and end the matter. Vikas Jaiswal- Oh, you told us many times, did we ever refuse you? Naveen Pandit- No, never, Vikas Bhai. Vikas Jaiswal- Till date, the Mayor has never called anyone and said, "Come, let's sit." Naveen Pandit- You are not our companion of today, but of 15 years. We've started feeling ashamed to talk. What should we talk to you about, tell us? Vikas Jaiswal- We understand your helplessness, my brother. We can understand your pain. Where you are stuck, in what predicament. On one side, Kapoor Sahab is busy there, in Govind Nagar, we can understand those people, you never work by bending so much, my brother. Today, we can understand your helplessness. Naveen Pandit - We are thinking of resigning. Yes, resign from the post of councillor, and say, "Brother, this is not going to feed us." These unnecessary troubles we are getting, they will stop, Vikas. Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, tell me, now we got information that the Mayor's father had an operation. Naveen Pandit- Operation? Vikas Jaiswal- Yes. Naveen Pandit- Not an operation, chemotherapy is happening. Chemotherapy is happening daily. Vikas Jaiswal- Yes, yes, some health issues were going on in Delhi. Naveen Pandit- Chemotherapy happens from Monday to Friday, Vikas Bhai, and mother is staying there. She will come now, she will come by train. Vikas Jaiswal- So, at this time, what was the need for Bunty to get all this done? Naveen Pandit- He is getting chemotherapy, not an operation. Vikas Jaiswal- I am saying that father is unwell, there is so much pain for father at home, so the mayor... what was the need for Bunty to do all this? Naveen Pandit- That's right. His own... Vikas Jaiswal- And Saurabh Dev understands this, Bablu Bhaiya Vajpayee ji was such a good friend of ours, his son is getting contract work done by Vikas Vajpayee. Don't we know what all is happening in the water department, and what is not happening? Naveen Pandit- You know everything, my brother, you are not new to the municipal corporation. You know everyone down to their hair. You also know everyone, you recognize every flying bird. Vikas Jaiswal- Man, if Vikas Jaiswal has ever taken even an inch of space, we fought for them last time, how much disrepute we brought to the party. Naveen Pandit- You are a councilor for three-four terms... You always used to dedicate yourself to the service of society, what are you saying? Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, they did not accept our Tapeshwari temple proposal for the temple, Maa Tapeshwari Devi temple. They did not accept the waterlogging at Phoolbagh on Birhana Road. They stopped the beautification work of Birhana Road. They didn't give money for the Baratshala. Oh man, we never asked for anything. Naveen Pandit- Our image shouldn't be built, let everyone else's be built. We are just... like, when we are needed, call us... use us like a tool and throw us away. Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, don't ruin your career because of these people, my brother. Naveen Pandit- I am going to Vaishno Devi, we are going. Navin Pandit- We are going to Vaishno Devi, will go on the 10th-12th. Vikas Jaiswal- Poor Pawan was in great pain, we explained to Pawan repeatedly. This is not Navin Bhaiya, he is being made to say this. Navin Pandit- Suppose two people were sitting with us, what kind of written agreement did we make or did something or... did something. But they should also speak everything with restraint on Facebook, man. Huh? Now he... Vikas Jaiswal- Has anything been written on Facebook? Navin Pandit- Yes, you know these people's habit, all this Facebook-WhatsApp... Oh, we can also make 50 people say it, but what's the need for us? Vikas Jaiswal- No, no, we'll talk now. Listen, someone must have written that for you, but listen, he respects you. Poor guy was crying. Navin Pandit- Brother, this small... Vikas Jaiswal- His wife is admitted, brother. Naveen Pandit- Oh man, tell me, God! Today Sandeep Paswan came, he told me. Vikas Jaiswal- Tell me, his wife was in emergency, in ICU. She has been admitted three times, everything is going on in his family too. Naveen Pandit- My brother, I don't understand. What should we do? Vikas Jaiswal- Let's go. Naveen Pandit- Understand, see you tomorrow. See you tomorrow at the Municipal Corporation. Vikas Jaiswal- You meet separately, not at the Municipal Corporation, meet somewhere else. Naveen Pandit- Okay, you come to Jageshwar, come to Govind Nagar, come to some place. Vikas Jaiswal- We will come, we will come tomorrow. We will sit one on one. Naveen Pandit- We will not go to the Municipal Corporation tomorrow, we will not go... Vikas Jaiswal- No-no, we will sit one on one, you guys, okay, you and I will sit. Naveen Pandit- Okay brother. Vikas Jaiswal- Good night. Now we tell you what the whole dispute is Complaints made from District President to Defense Minister and CM, yet the dispute was not resolved The house was in session at Kanpur Municipal Corporation on December 26, 2025. During this, councillors Pawan Gupta and Ankit Maurya created a ruckus over their demands. After the ruckus, the Mayor had expelled both councillors from the house meetings for three days. In protest of the expulsion, four other BJP councillors also came out in support of the two councillors, accusing the mayor and her son of not providing budget for regional development works, which further deepened the dispute. 6 councilors opened a front against the mayor and first presented their case before Kanpur District President Anil Dixit. When the dispute did not stop even after this, they took their matter to Yogendra Upadhyay, the minister in charge of Kanpur. The minister in charge also spoke to the 6 councillors and understood the whole matter, but the matter did not calm down. After this, the 6 councillors opposing the mayor met State President Pankaj Chaudhary, and not only that, the councillors even reached Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to present their case, but the dispute did not stop. After this, on June 18, councillor Pawan Gupta complained about the mayor by giving a letter to the CM during a program at the CSA campus. After a complaint to the CM, the dispute escalated again, and BJP councillors, led by councillor group leader Naveen Pandit, unitedly held a press conference on behalf of the mayor and demanded the expulsion of all six councillors from the party. Following this, an audio clip of Naveen Pandit, the leader of the councillor group who held a press conference against the rebel councillors, has now surfaced.

stories.title: Brother arrested after sister's murder:Suspected affair behind killing; hospital tips off police
stories.summary: In Meerut, a brother, angered by his sister's affair, shot and killed her. He shot his sister in the head. As soon as she was shot, the sister fell there, covered in blood. After shooting her, the brother remained hidden in the house. When the mother arrived, the brother and other family members rushed the daughter towards the hospital. During this time, blood kept flowing from the house to the hospital. They reached Jagdamba Hospital at 7:10 AM on Saturday. They told the doctors that the daughter was injured from a fall. However, due to it being a gunshot wound, the doctors informed the police and started treatment. Aksa (21) died there. Being a case of a gunshot, the police took cognizance of the matter and investigated. It was found that the family members had concealed the incident. The accused brother, Aarish (23), has been arrested. Also, at his instance, a .315 bore country-made pistol used in the murder has been recovered. The accused has confessed to the murder during interrogation. The incident took place in Zakir Colony, under the Lohia Nagar police station area. See 3 pictures Mother said I was in the bathroom Aksha's mother Asifa said- I didn't see anything. I had just gone to the toilet after offering prayers. When I came out, my daughter was lying covered in blood. I immediately put a sheet over her. The mother tearfully said- I and the children live alone in this house. Aksha has studied up to 8th grade. Aksha doesn't have a father. He died 12 years ago. Aksha is the only sister among four brothers. The eldest son is Arish and Aksha is second. While Kaif is third. Then there are Ahad and Junaid. Read what SP City said SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said that on Saturday morning at 7:10 AM, Jagdamba Hospital informed the concerned police station that an injured young woman had been brought to the hospital. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot. It was found to be a gunshot case. The girl had been shot. After this, the CO Kotwali himself went to the girl's house for investigation, and during questioning and investigation, it was revealed that her own brother, Aarish, had shot the girl around 6 AM. After this, the family members took the girl to the hospital, where she died during treatment. The reasons for the murder are also being investigated. Suspicion of murder due to an affair From the police interrogation so far, it appears that Arish killed his sister Aksa on suspicion of a love affair. Aksa used to talk to a young man from the neighborhood. The family had become aware of this. Therefore, the family wanted to arrange their daughter's marriage. But Aksa had refused to marry. The teenager continued to talk to that young man. According to the police, there was an argument in the family over this matter on Friday night as well. It is suspected that due to this, the brother killed her on Saturday morning.

stories.title: Ex-IAS claims ₹5 cr gold-plated Ramcharitmanas Missing:Says Champat Rai gave no receipt; Kedarnath-Badrinath also face donation theft allegations
stories.summary: Amid the donation theft controversy at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, former Union Home Secretary Laxmi Narayan has claimed that his gold-plated Ramcharitmanas has gone missing. He said he had donated a 1.25-quintal Ramcharitmanas to the Ram Temple Trust on 8 April, 2024, but has not received an acknowledgment receipt to date. He further alleged that the Ramcharitmanas disappeared from the temple 3-4 months later. The 1,000-page Ramcharitmanas is coated with 24-carat gold and is valued at Rs 5 crore. Speaking to a media channel, he said, When I reached Ayodhya, Champat Rai made me wait for nine hours. I folded my hands and said, 'Sir, this is the savings of my entire lifetime. Please ensure that the Ramcharitmanas is kept in the temple.' He replied, 'Many people give me jewellery and various other items. Should I keep displaying only such things? The former IAS officer said he contacted Temple Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Mishra and Trust member Gopal Rao, but nothing happened. He then visited Ayodhya again. After waiting for four hours, he finally met Champat Rai, who allegedly told him, 'I can't do anything. Go wherever you want.' Meanwhile, on Saturday, the Ram Mandir Trust released the agenda for its meeting scheduled for 6 July. The meeting will decide on the resignations of Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra. It will also discuss the preliminary SIT report and issues related to temple management. Reacting to reports of Champat Rai's resignation from the Trust, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand took a jibe, saying, Will resigning after theft in the court of such a great deity be enough to escape? What kind of drama is this? You will be beaten. If the government does not send them to jail and ensure proper punishment, the public will beat them. After Ram Mandir, donation theft allegations surface at Kedarnath and Badrinath Following the allegations of donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, similar allegations have now surfaced at the Kedarnath and Badrinath temples. Sandeep Khatri, president of the religious organisation Bhairav Sena, has written to the Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC), accusing the personal assistant to the BKTC chairman of theft. After receiving the complaint, BKTC CEO Sohan Singh Rangar issued notices to the personal assistant and all staff on duty, seeking their response within three days. CCTV footage from the temples has also been secured for investigation. BKTC Chairman Hemant Dwivedi said the temple committee is taking the matter seriously. Notices have been issued to the employees against whom allegations have been made, asking them to submit explanations. If any employee is found guilty, strict legal action will be taken. No statement has yet been issued by Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. The government is waiting for the temple committee's report on the matter. Ram Mandir donation theft, Avinash gets the biggest share, ₹20.39 lakh recovered Note: Avinash was also found with 112 US dollars, two gold chains, one ring and silver jewellery.

stories.title: Govt offering up to ₹1.08 lakh for installing solar panels:UP administration plans to reduce public power bill; here's how to apply
stories.summary: You can make your home's electricity bill 'zero'. This means you will use the same amount of electricity, but you won't have to pay the bill. For this, you will have to install solar panels on the roof of your house. The cost is also not too high, as the government provides a subsidy of up to Rs 1.08 lakh. You will have to install solar panels according to your home's electricity load. It is important that you ensure the quality of the panels is good. What things should be kept in mind while installing a solar plant? How many watts of panel is appropriate to install? Read in this report Understand how the electricity bill becomes zero Alok Srivastava, who lives in the old city, was paying an electricity bill of 3 to 4 thousand rupees every month. He installed a 4 KW solar panel on the roof of his house. He says - when the sun shines well, the panels generate about 25 units of electricity every day. This amounts to 750 units in a month. Now, if he consumes up to 750 units of electricity, only the meter charge is added to the bill, which is around 300 rupees. If he consumes more than 750 units, then he has to pay the bill at the rate of ₹7 per unit. Government provides subsidy based on load Bank provides loans for solar panels Installing a 3 kW solar system costs between ₹1.68 lakh to ₹1.93 lakh, depending on the brand. This includes the cost of solar panels, inverter, structure, wiring, and installation. If you don't have the full amount, you can also take a solar loan from any government or private bank. Interest rates of government banks are around 7%. Whereas, private banks charge interest from 9% to 12%. Upon receiving the subsidy, you can deposit it into your loan account. This will reduce your monthly EMI and your total cost will be around ₹60,000 to ₹85,000. Keep these things in mind before installing solar panels Before installing solar panels at home, it is important to check some important things. A 1-kilowatt system requires about 100 square feet of space. Whereas, a 3-kilowatt system requires 300 square feet of space. Choose a solar system based on your needs Install solar panels in a place that receives good sunlight throughout the day. Shade from trees or buildings can reduce electricity generation by 30-40%. Panels are quite heavy, so checking the strength of the roof is also important. Regular cleaning and maintenance should also be done so that the system continues to provide better electricity. Off-grid systems do not receive subsidies Solar consultant Manish Mishra explains - Solar systems work in two ways. One- On-grid and Second- Off-grid. What is an On-grid Solar System? This system is connected to the electricity department's grid. During the day, electricity generated by solar is used in the home. Excess electricity goes into the grid via a net meter. At night, electricity is received from the grid. At the end of the month, the bill is generated based on the electricity sent to and received from the grid. This system also shuts down during power outages. It is cheap because it does not incur battery costs. PM Surya Ghar Yojana and UP government subsidies are available on this system. A 3 kW solar plant gets a subsidy of ₹1.08 lakh Note: No subsidy is available for solar plants with a capacity above 3 kW. What is an Off-Grid Solar System This system is not connected to the electricity department's grid. It requires a battery. It works similarly to an inverter system installed in a home. The only difference is that instead of storing electricity from the government grid (electricity department), it stores electricity generated from solar power in the battery. This system keeps the supply on during power outages. Due to the battery, its cost is higher than an on-grid system. A normal battery needs to be replaced every 5-7 years. Lithium-ion batteries can last for 10-12 years. These are even more expensive. Subsidies are not available for this system. 2,000 Rooftop Solar Systems are being installed daily in UP Uttar Pradesh ranks first in the country in terms of rooftop solar, meaning installing solar plants on the roofs of houses. Here, about 2,000 rooftop solar systems are being installed daily. More than 6,000 registered vendors are working for this. From February 2024 to June 2026, more than 5.57 lakh solar systems have been installed. These include 9200 government and 691 private commercial buildings, and solar plants have also been installed on the land of water tanks and tube wells/pumping stations being built under the Jal Jeevan Mission. For this, more than 3602 crore rupees have been provided as subsidy by the central government and more than 1200 crore rupees by the state government.

stories.title: Day 3 of UP-TET 2026:Strict checks continue, female candidates asked to remove hairpins, jewellery; 26 held for alleged cheating
stories.summary: Saturday marked the third and final day of the Teacher Eligibility Test (UP-TET) 2026 in UP. Candidates were allowed entry into the examination centers from 7:15 AM to 8:45 AM. During this time, admit cards were checked, biometric details were matched, and retina scans were performed. The first shift examination will run from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM, and the second shift examination will run from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM. In Gorakhpur, female candidates were asked to remove hair claws, hairpins, and jewellery. In Hathras, belts and shoes were removed for checking. In Kanpur, women's bangles were removed. In Lalitpur, a woman's amulet and necklace were removed from her neck. In Hathras, a female candidate from Aligarh was denied entry for arriving two minutes late. As the gate did not open, she returned disappointed. In Raebareli, a dog suddenly appeared in front of a student's car who was going to take the exam. In an attempt to save it, the car went out of control and fell into a canal. The student and her father were pulled out by nearby people. After this, both left for the examination center in another car. Today, on the final day, 3,78,655 candidates will appear for the examination. In two days, 26 cheaters have been caught from across the state. Among these, 15 candidates were caught on the first day and 9 on the second day. As many as 955 examination centers have been set up in 60 districts of the state. A total of 19.94 lakh candidates are taking the examination, including 1,85,791 in-service teachers.

stories.title: Wife kills husband, buries body in bathroom, covers with tiles:Uses same bathroom daily, misleads family for 45 days
stories.summary: A man from Bharatpur was murdered by his wife. The accused woman buried the body in the bathroom of the house itself. She had tiles laid over it. The accused continued to use this same bathroom for bathing. She misled people for about 45 days. On Friday (July 3), the entire matter was exposed. The police recovered the body of Surendra Kumar Sharma (44) buried in the bathroom. The police also arrested the accused woman Ruby. The incident is from Renuka Dham Colony in the Sikandra police station area of Agra. First see - pictures of the crime scene... Marriage happened 16 years ago, there was discord between the two Surendra Kumar Sharma (44), originally from Bharatpur, Rajasthan, was living in Renuka Dham Colony in Dahatora, Sikandra area of Agra, along with his mother, wife Ruby and their two daughters. He was married to Ruby from Etawah in 2010. The couple has two daughters, Ridhi (13) and Siddhi (9). His brother Anil Sharma said there had been long-standing disputes between the husband and wife. Now know the complete matter Information given to brother-in-law on 18th May Surendra’s brother Anil Sharma said that Ruby called him on the morning of May 18. She informed him that there was some police-related issue at home and asked him to take away their mother and both daughters. When Anil tried to get full details, she did not explain anything clearly. She only said not to come home and added that she had made the mother and children sit at a nearby shop, from where they should be taken. Second call claiming Surendra had left home Anil said he was about to reach his home in Awadhpuri with the mother and both daughters when Ruby called again. She said Surendra had forcibly opened the house lock, taken ₹5,000, and left after a quarrel. She further claimed that he had said he would call after 2–3 days to inform them of his whereabouts. Ruby stayed at brother-in-law’s house for 7–8 days On the evening of May 19, Ruby again contacted her brother-in-law Anil Sharma and said she was not feeling comfortable staying there and should also be taken to where the children were. That night, Anil brought her to his house. Ruby then stayed there with both children for around 7–8 days. Missing report filed on May 26 During this period, there was no trace of Surendra. Anil Sharma and other family members repeatedly questioned Ruby, but she kept misleading them with different versions of events. When no clue was found despite continuous efforts, Anil Sharma lodged a missing person report on May 26 for his brother. Told brother-in-law - I have buried the body in the house Anil Sharma said that he later asked Ruby directly about Surendra’s whereabouts. She then told him that she had buried him inside the bathroom of the house. He further stated that on June 27, when suspicion increased, he brought his mother from Surendra’s house and took her to Bharatpur, where he obtained the bank account statement. He alleged that Ruby was using the pension money credited to the mother’s account. According to Anil, on Friday around 6 am, Ruby called him again and asked him to come to the house. When he reached Renuka Dham Colony, he asked about Surendra. Initially, Ruby avoided answering, but when he reassured her and asked her to tell the truth, saying he would support her if she was in trouble, she became emotional and confessed everything. She said Surendra had hanged himself and that in panic she buried the body under the bathroom floor of the house. Police action and arrest According to Agra Police, during investigation, CCTV footage from around the house was checked and Ruby was seen present during various moments, but she never disclosed the truth. She was arrested on Friday. Sleeping pills in food and concealment of body During interrogation, Ruby told police that on the night of May 17, she allegedly mixed more than a dozen sleeping pills into kheer and served it to her husband Surendra. After the incident, she buried the body under the bathroom floor, got it plastered, and later installed tiles over it. She continued using the same bathroom for bathing, while keeping the concealment hidden for a long period.

stories.title: BJP chief Nitin Nabin waves sword during roadshow:Muslim women join; 25 feet garland presented by bulldozer
stories.summary: Nitin Nabin will make his first visit to Uttar Pradesh as the BJP's national president on Saturday. He is scheduled to stay in Lucknow for 36 hours. More than 50 reception points have been set up between the airport and the BJP state headquarters, with over 50,000 party workers and office-bearers notified for the welcome. More than 1,00,000 posters and banners have also been put up across the city. On Saturday, Nabin will attend a meeting at a hotel in Lucknow with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary, along with MPs, MLAs and ministers. On Sunday, he will visit the RSS headquarters, Bharati Bhavan, for discussions with regional pracharak Anil Kumar and state pracharak Kaushal Kumar. The visit is expected to focus on devising a strategy to counter the Samajwadi Party's 'PDA' formula, which the BJP believes hurt its prospects in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Discussions will also centre on preparing the party's roadmap for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, to secure a third consecutive term. The party is also expected to formulate its response to the recent controversy over alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir. Navin will also hold his first interaction with the BJP's newly announced Uttar Pradesh leadership team, unveiled nine days ago. The line-up includes young leaders such as Abhijat Mishra, Rajni Pandey, Rahul Valmiki, Yatendra Sharma and Ankur Sharma. Efforts to improve coordination between the government, the party organisation and the RSS are also expected to be on the agenda. See pictures of the BJP National President's welcome... Nitin Nabin to stay in Lucknow for 36 hours Nitin Nabin will be in Lucknow for 36 hours. On Saturday, he will hold a meeting with MPs, MLAs and ministers at Hotel Taj in the presence of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and State BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary. On Sunday, he will visit the RSS headquarters, Bharati Bhavan, where he will meet Regional Pracharak Anil Kumar and Prant Pracharak Kaushal Kumar. The BJP chief's visit is primarily aimed at formulating a strategy to counter the Samajwadi Party's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak) formula, which the BJP believes hurt its prospects in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The party is also expected to prepare its roadmap for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with the goal of securing a third consecutive term in power. The recent controversy over the alleged theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple is also expected to be discussed, and the organisation is likely to send out a fresh message on the issue. Nabin will also interact for the first time with the BJP's new Uttar Pradesh state team, announced nine days ago. The new team includes young leaders such as Abhijat Mishra, Rajni Pandey, Rahul Valmiki, Yatendra Sharma and Ankur Sharma. The visit is also expected to focus on strengthening coordination between the government, the party organisation and the RSS.

stories.title: Kanpur sees wettest day in 15 years:Rain alert issued for 28 UP districts
stories.summary: The monsoon continues to remain active across Uttar Pradesh with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a rain alert for 28 districts on Saturday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely. Most districts saw sunny spells in the morning with intermittent cloud cover. Kanpur recorded its wettest 3rd July in 15 years, receiving 108 mm of rainfall. The previous record was 101 mm, logged on 1 July 2011. Rain lashed 20 districts across the state on Friday. In Mathura, heavy showers left several roads submerged under up to a foot of water, causing vehicles to break down. A railway underpass was flooded up to neck level, disrupting movement. The state received an average of 6.2 mm of rainfall over the past 24 hours, around 9 per cent above the normal 5.7 mm. However, cumulative rainfall since 1 June stands at 64.5 mm, which is 43 per cent below the seasonal normal of 112.5 mm. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the monsoon has now become active over Uttar Pradesh and persistent rainfall is expected in the coming days. Temperatures have dropped by up to 8°C, and similar weather conditions are likely to continue for the next week. However, he added that the state, including Lucknow, is still expected to receive below-normal rainfall during the monsoon season.

stories.title: Firing at Kashi Vishwanath Temple:PAC jawan's carbine falls, two shots accidentally fired; 3 injured
stories.summary: On Saturday morning at 7:30 AM, a carbine fell from the hand of a PAC jawan at the gate of Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Following this, two rounds were fired from the carbine. Fortunately, the bullets directly hit the road. Subsequently, gravel and small stones bounced up and hit three people. Police personnel present at the scene took all three to the divisional hospital. According to doctors, everyone's condition is currently out of danger. The injured have been identified as Nikki Gupta, Rambabu, and Vikas Yadav. All three injured are flower and garland vendors who operate outside the temple. According to doctors, they are in a stable condition and out of danger. They sustained injuries after being hit by stone fragments dislodged by the bullets. The incident occurred at VIP Gate No. 4 of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The sudden gunfire in the middle of the crowd triggered panic, with people scrambling for safety. For a few moments, no one could understand what had happened. On hearing the shots, security personnel immediately rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control. They informed people that the rounds had been fired accidentally and assured them that the situation was under control.
