stories.title: Missing Class 9 student found following post on Facebook:Youth ran away two years ago after fight with father
stories.summary: A ninth-grade student who went missing about two years ago from the Gulriha police station area of Gorakhpur was found in Ajmer, Rajasthan. A missing person report was filed at Gulriha police station on September 3, 2024, and a police team was engaged in the search for the student. The student's family informed the police after seeing their son's photo on Facebook. When the police investigated, they found the location to be Ajmer, Rajasthan. After this, a police team left for Ajmer on Tuesday after talking to the local police there. Upon reaching there, it was found that the student, Shashikant, was working in a hotel. Gulriha police, along with the local police, made contact with the student on Thursday. After this, the police arranged a conversation between the boy and his family. During the conversation on the mobile, the student and his family members started crying. After completing necessary legal procedures, the police left for Gorakhpur with the boy. The team arrived with the student around 12 PM on Friday and handed him over to his family. Know the full story Shashikant, the 15-year-old younger son of Tarkeshwar Pandey, a resident of Sneh City Colony, Mugalaha, under Gulriha police station area, left for school on the morning of September 3, 2024, and did not return. The family members searched for a long time. They inquired at the school and with relatives but no trace was found. By evening, they reached the police station and filed a missing person report. In the complaint, the family expressed apprehension of kidnapping. According to information, a day earlier, the father had scolded Shashikant for his studies, which had made him very angry. He was not eating dinner at night either. After much persuasion from his mother, he ate and went to sleep. He woke up in the morning and quietly got ready for school. He had breakfast, took his lunch, and left. Concern grew when he didn't return from school Everyone was thinking that he had gone to study. But he did not return home long after school was over. Family members searched for him nearby. When they inquired at the school, they found out that he had not even reached the school. There was a fear of kidnapping His parents also inquired at the homes of friends and relatives, but there was no trace of their son. After which, they feared kidnapping. Father saw photo on Facebook 10 days ago According to information, about 10 days ago, Shashikant's father saw Shashikant in a post on Facebook. He immediately informed the police. As soon as the information was received, the police team immediately became active. They tried to find the location of that ID with the help of surveillance. The investigation revealed the location of Ajmer, Rajasthan. The police first tried to contact them by phone. Police team reached Ajmer Even after many attempts, when contact could not be established from here, a team left for Ajmer on Tuesday. After reaching there on Wednesday morning, a thorough search was conducted with the help of photos. Then the location of a hotel was found. When the police reached that hotel, Shashikant was seen working there. He was recovered with the help of local police around 9 AM on Thursday morning. After completing the proceedings, the police arranged for him to speak with his family. After that, around 12 PM on Friday afternoon, the police brought him to Gorakhpur and handed him over to his family after necessary action. Reached Rajasthan to meet YouTuber 'Indian Hacker' During police interrogation, Shashikant stated that he is a very big fan of YouTuber 'Indian Hacker'. He used to watch his videos a lot. He lives in Ajmer, Rajasthan. I left home upset to meet him. After going to Rajasthan, when I couldn't meet him, I started looking for work in a hotel.

stories.title: 38-year-old man rapes minor sister:Accused tells police he saw his wife in the victim
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man who repeatedly raped his minor sister for about one-and-a-half years in Fatehpur was sent to jail by the police on Thursday evening around 4 pm. While being taken to jail, the accused said, “I used to see my deceased wife in my younger sister, which is why I raped her.” According to the police, the accused had beaten his wife to death about three years ago for refusing to consume drugs. After that, he went to jail. The rape-accused was released from jail in June 2024 and returned home. Since then, he raped his 16-year-old biological sister. The sister complained to her family members many times, but no one believed her. After this, with the help of her friends, the victim made a video of the accused committing the rape and showed it to her family. After watching the video, the family was stunned. The case is from a village in the Thariyaon police station area, 28 km away from the district headquarters. Based on the complaint filed by the victim's other brother's wife, the police registered an FIR on Wednesday under several serious sections, including the POCSO Act. Case filed on sister-in-law's complaint, accused sent to jail after medical examination Based on the complaint of the younger sister-in-law, Thariyaon Police Station registered a case under several serious sections, including the POCSO Act. The police arrested the accused and presented him in court, from where he was sent to jail. The victim has undergone a medical examination and the police are collecting other evidence. Father died 7 years ago According to information received from family members, the victim's family includes her mother, middle brother, and his wife. Her father died seven years ago due to illness. The victim is currently studying in high school, while the accused worked as a laborer. We will ensure the strictest punishment for the accused, says Station In-charge Thariyawan Police Station in-charge Inspector Shamsher Bahadur said A 16-year-old sister has accused her 38-year-old biological brother of rape. Video evidence has also been provided. Medical examination has confirmed the rape. A case has been registered under the POCSO Act and other sections, and the accused has been sent to jail.

stories.title: 40-year-old influencer stabbed to death:Husband injures himself to mislead the police; dispute over land registration cited as reason
stories.summary: Social media influencer Nisha Chauhan (40) was stabbed to death by her husband in Meerut at 6 AM on Friday morning. After the killing, Nisha's husband Pradeep Chauhan (42) inflicted several wounds on himself. He was severely injured. At the time, witnesses said the couple's children came out of the house screaming. When neighbors entered the house, Nisha was lying on the floor, covered in blood. A short distance away, Pradeep was writhing in pain. Police, who arrived after being informed, took both to the hospital. There, doctors declared the female influencer dead. The reason for the incident is said to be a dispute over the registration of a 1,170 sq ft plot of land. According to police sources, the land was to be registered today (Friday) itself. Nisha wanted the registration to be in her name, but Pradeep was not ready. Forensic teams and officials reached the spot. They collected evidence. Police questioned the children. CCTV footage from around the house is also being scanned. The incident took place in Harra town, under the Sarurpur Police Station area. See 3 pictures Dragged from the bedroom to the hall, stabbed with knives So far, in the investigation, the police have found that there was a dispute between Nisha and Pradeep. Pradeep dragged Nisha from the bedroom to the hall. He attacked her with a knife. He also attacked her throat. Nisha fell, covered in blood. After this, Pradeep also stabbed himself with a knife. 24K Followers on Instagram Nisha Chauhan's Instagram ID is named rajputnisha_5m. The name written is Nisha Rajput. She has 24,4000 followers. She has made 960 posts so far. She used to follow 10 people. In the bio, 'Your love', 'Target 50 thousand', 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Jai Bhawani' are written. A link to her YouTube channel is also provided.

stories.title: 24-year-old Army aspirant found dead:Family cries foul, expresses suspicion of murder
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man, who was preparing for Army recruitment, was found dead, hanging from a noose in an under-construction house in Jangal Mahadeva village, under the Chauri Chaura Police Station limits of Gorakhpur, late on Thursday night. As the body was found about 200 meters away from the deceased's home, family members and villagers have expressed suspicion of murder. Police have sent the body for post-mortem and started investigating the matter. The deceased was identified as Kush Chaudhary, a resident of the village. Kush's father, Gaurishankar Chaudhary, had passed away. He was the younger of two brothers and was unmarried. According to family members, Kush was preparing for Army recruitment. His elder brother, Dinanath Chaudhary, is a sanitation worker in Brahmpur block. Late on Thursday night, around 11 PM, villagers saw the youth's body hanging from a noose on the doorframe of an under-construction house outside the village. Upon receiving information about the incident, Chauri Chaura Station House Officer Inspector Ved Prakash Sharma arrived at the scene, took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem after necessary procedures. The police also inspected the incident site. No signs of injury were found anywhere. Meanwhile, the family members have not expressed suspicion on anyone. Station House Officer Ved Prakash stated that the exact cause of death will only be known after the post-mortem.

stories.title: Security tightened for UP-TET:15 solver gang members caught, constable dies en route to duty
stories.summary: UP-TET 2026 entered its second day on Friday amid heightened security across Uttar Pradesh following the recent teacher eligibility test paper leak in Maharashtra. Candidates underwent admit card verification, biometric authentication and retina scans before entering exam centres. Entry for the first shift was allowed between 7:15 am and 8:45 am. The first paper was held from 9:30 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will run from 2:30 pm to 5 pm. At a centre in Lalitpur, a woman candidate arrived wearing a veil, saying she had accompanied her brother-in-law. In Gorakhpur, women candidates were asked to remove hair clips, hairpins, bangles and jewellery, while men underwent belt checks. In Hathras, women were asked to untie their hair buns, and men removed their shoes during frisking. In Lucknow, a woman constable gave a candidate a lift to her exam centre on a scooter. In Basti, a 51-year-old head constable on exam duty was killed in a road accident early Friday morning. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission is monitoring the examination for the first time through an AI-integrated command and control centre, while intelligence agencies remain on alert. On the first day of the exam, held on Thursday, 15 impersonators were caught attempting to write the test on behalf of other candidates. The attendance stood at 84.76%, with 6,84,614 of the 8,07,636 registered candidates appearing across both shifts. The examination is being conducted at 955 centres across 60 districts and will continue on 4 July. Nearly 19.9 lakh candidates are expected to appear, including 17.7 lakh from Uttar Pradesh and 2,27,481 from other states. Among them 1,85,791 are in-service teachers. See photos from outside the examination centres.

stories.title: VIDEO | LPG tanker crash footage surfaces:Generator spark ignited gas leak; 5 died in the incident
stories.summary: A video has emerged of an LPG tanker colliding with a toll booth in Kaushambi. It shows that the tanker exploded after hitting the toll plaza, and gas started leaking. Within seconds, gas spread 30-40 feet. A generator was running right at the toll plaza. The gas reached the generator and there was a loud explosion. Fire spread everywhere. Flames rose 25-30 feet high. The accident occurred on 26 June at 6:38 AM at the Sirohi Toll Plaza under Kokhraj police station limits. Five people, including the tanker driver, had died. The driver was burnt alive inside the tanker. While the remaining three toll workers and a passerby died during treatment. One injured person is undergoing treatment in Prayagraj. The CCTV footage emerged on Thursday night at 10 PM. 4 pictures of the accident After the accident, all the CCTVs and systems installed at the toll plaza were destroyed. Later, experts recovered CCTV footage from the server. The CCTV shows that after the LPG tanker exploded, a white smoke-like gas spread. In a few seconds, the gas covered the entire toll plaza. Then, a spark from the generator ignited the fire. The fire engulfed the entire toll plaza. Sihori Toll Plaza was burnt to ashes. Sixteen bikes and two cars parked in the yard also caught fire and were burnt. The driver's bones were found in the tanker After the accident, the fire brigade team that arrived on information brought the fire under control after about 30 minutes of effort. When the team inspected the tanker, the bones of driver Dharmendra Dubey (40) were found. The tanker was going from Kanpur towards Pratapgarh. Toll employee Alok Singh also died in the accident. Toll employee Anil Kumar, a resident of Handia, died on July 1 during treatment. On July 2, two other injured persons died. These include Heeramani Singh (29), a resident of Rajapur, Raebareli, and Krishnapal Maurya (23), a resident of Katheli village in Sidhi, Madhya Pradesh. Toll employee Sanjay Nirmal said, "There was light rain for 10 minutes before the accident. Don't know what happened suddenly that the entire vehicle fell with a thud. The fire, fuelled by a gas leak, spread to the yard and toilet adjacent to the plaza. Supervisor Alok Pandey, who was in the toilet, was severely burnt. A video of him running on the road has also surfaced.

stories.title: RSS on Ram Mandir theft:‘Grave sin’; guilty must be punished, Vinay Katiyar says Champat, Anil may face jail
stories.summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) on Friday issued its first statement on the alleged theft of donations from the donation boxes at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale described the incident as "unfortunate" and said it had deeply hurt the faith and sentiments of lakhs of Lord Ram devotees. He said that whoever is found guilty in the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe should face strict punishment. "The theft of money collected in the donation boxes of the Ram Lalla Mandir is unfortunate. It has hurt the emotions and devotion of Ram devotees. Whoever is found guilty in the SIT investigation must be given stringent punishment," Hosabale said. Vinay Katiyar alleges embezzlement of temple funds Meanwhile, in Ayodhya, senior BJP leader Vinay Katiyar alleged that there had been a clear embezzlement of temple funds. He claimed that Ram Mandir Trust former General Secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr. Anil Mishra, and invited trust member Gopal Rao had escaped legal action for now. "It is clear that there has been embezzlement of money. Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao have somehow escaped and have not gone to jail. They may end up in jail later," Katiyar said. Meanwhile, Ram Mandir donation theft accused Avinash Shukla has been taken into police custody for 24 hours. Police reached Ayodhya Jail at 9 am on Friday and left for Pratapgarh with him. Avinash is originally from Pratapgarh district. He worked as part of the team that counted donations at the Ram Mandir and lived in a rented room in Ayodhya. Police recovered ₹20 lakh in cash, 1,000 US dollars, jewellery and a box labelled 'Ram Rajya Fund' from his room. According to sources, police learnt during questioning that Avinash hid the gold and silver jewellery, along with cash donated to the Ram Mandir. Investigators are expected to take him to the locations identified by him to recover the items. Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) has once again summoned trustee Dr Anil Mishra and invited trust member Gopal Rao for questioning today. They have been asked to bring their bank details and documents related to the appointment of Ram Mandir staff. The SIT had already questioned both men behind closed doors for five hours on Thursday. Preparation underway for bulldozer action at accused's homes Meanwhile, the Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) is preparing to demolish newly built houses linked to Ram Mandir donation theft accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The ADA has also issued a notice to Lavkush's wife, Supriya Mishra. However, Lavkush's wife said they had not received any notice. She claimed the house was built with an approved plan and said her only prayer was for her husband to return home safely.

stories.title: India's first urban ropeway ready in Varanasi:45-minute journey cut to 16, fares start from ₹10
stories.summary: The country's first public transport ropeway is ready in Varanasi. This high-tech service could start around Dev Deepawali (November 24, 2026). Built at a cost of ₹800 crores, this ropeway will take you from Cantt Railway Station to near Kashi Vishwanath Dham (Godoulia) in just 16 minutes. The same route takes 45 minutes by road. After Mexico and La Paz-El Alto in Bolivia, Varanasi is going to become the third city in the world where ropeway will be used as a public transportation system. Why is Varanasi Ropeway special worldwide? Solution to traffic in densely populated areas: This 3.85-kilometer long urban ropeway will pass over extremely densely populated and narrow areas. It is estimated that road traffic will be reduced by up to 40% once it starts. Excellent Capacity: Cable cars (cabins) will operate in both directions in this aerial corridor. 3,000 passengers will be able to travel in one direction, and a total of 6,000 passengers per hour combining both directions. Approximately 96,000 people will benefit from it daily. If compared to other cities in the world- Claim: Ropeway corridor will reduce traffic by 40% According to the Varanasi Development Authority (VDA), the launch of this ropeway, passing over the city's busiest and narrowest areas, will reduce ground traffic by up to 40 per cent. A total of five stations have been built along this corridor. 1. Varanasi Cantt Railway Station (Starting Terminal) It has been designed as a state-of-the-art multi-modal transport hub. This will allow passengers to alight from the train and directly board the ropeway without exiting the station premises. It will feature airport-style lounges, high-tech digital cloak rooms, and short-stay mini-hotels (refreshing rooms) for pilgrims staying only a few hours. 2. Kashi Vidyapeeth Station This will be a major stop for students, researchers, and local shopkeepers. The 15-20 minutes wasted in traffic jams on the road between Cantt and Vidyapeeth will now be eliminated. 3. Rath Yatra Station Varanasi's main commercial hub, connecting large textile markets like Luxa Road, Bhelupur, and Sigra. Tourists staying in these commercial areas and hotels outside the main temple area of Godaulia will be able to catch a cable car directly from here and reach the ghats in just a few minutes. 4. Girjaghar Station (technical Stop Only) Here, the cable car doors will not open for passengers, nor will tickets be available. Actually, due to the narrow and sharp turns between Rath Yatra and Godaulia, the cable car cannot turn directly at 90 degrees. Therefore, this station has been built as a 'turning point' and emergency backup to turn the cable car in the air at a safe angle of 65 degrees. 5. Godowlia Chowk (Last Terminal) From here, Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Dashashwamedh Ghat will be just 400 meters away. Earlier, one had to face severe traffic jams while traveling from Cantt to here by auto or e-rickshaw, but now the journey will be easier. To showcase Varanasi's cultural identity, the exterior of this station is being decorated with Chunar red stones and carved glass. Travel in an AC Cabin for just ₹10 Keeping in mind the pockets of the common public, the journey on this high-tech ropeway has been kept very affordable. According to the official fare list released on 23 June, the minimum fare has been fixed at ₹10. This will increase based on the distance of the station under a 'slab system'. The fare from Cantt to Vidyapeeth is ₹10. Then, the fare will increase by ₹10 for each subsequent station. For the entire journey from Varanasi Cantt to the last station, Godowlia Chowk, ₹50 will have to be paid. However, this seems cheaper when compared to road traffic jams and e-rickshaw or auto fares. E-rickshaws or autos charge ₹30 to ₹40 per passenger for this distance. In heavy traffic, more than 45 minutes are also wasted. However, there is a provision for a 1 per cent to 5 per cent increase in ropeway fares every year on April 1st. 20% Discount on 'Kashi Smart Pass' Keeping in mind local shopkeepers and students of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth, the Kashi Smart Pass System is being implemented. Using this QR-based smart card will provide a direct 20% discount on every trip. With the smart pass, the entire journey from Cantt to Godaulia, which costs ₹50, will be covered for just ₹40. Meanwhile, the ₹10 fare from Vidyapeeth to Rath Yatra will become ₹8. Those who get a fixed monthly pass will receive a huge discount of up to 30 per cent. This will benefit daily commuters. Tourists can book entire cabins There is also a provision to book an entire cable car for corporate VIPs, special VVIP families, and luxury tourists. If a whole group or family wants to travel privately alone, the entire ropeway cabin can be booked at a rate of ₹2,000 per trip. If a travel agency, hotel, or institution makes a group booking in advance, they will receive a discount. They will only have to pay ₹1200 per cabin. Whether power cuts or a storm comes, the ropeway is safe International safety standards have been adopted in the Varanasi ropeway, so that passengers do not face problems during power cuts or storms. In case of a main power cut, the entire system will shift to automatic generator and heavy-duty inverter backup within one second. Even if the entire power system fails, 'emergency diesel engines' have been installed as backup at every station. Their job will be to safely pull all cable cars stuck in the air to the next station, so that passengers do not remain stranded in the air. 'Anemometers' have been installed on the towers to measure wind speed. If the wind speed exceeds 65 to 70 km per hour, the system will automatically slow down the cable car's speed by sounding an alarm. After this, passengers will be disembarked at safe stations and operations will be stopped.

stories.title: DSO rejects land mafia links:UP PCS officer says 'Mother sold 17 bighas for ₹68 lakhs'
stories.summary: "I didn't even know that an FIR had been filed in Saharanpur. I got to know from the news on Thursday morning. When I checked, I found out that my mother herself had filed a case against me and my family. The police neither investigated nor tried to find out the truth." “An attempt was made to tarnish my image. How can I have a connection with land mafias? My mother sold 17 bighas of land to a person from Dehradun, and that money came into her account.” This is what Dr. Seema Chaudhary, a 2017 batch PCS (Provincial Civil Service) officer and DSO (District Supply Officer) of Hapur, has to say. The woman officer's mother, Munesh Rani, filed an FIR against her in Saharanpur on June 30. The Sarsawa police station has registered a case against 5 people, including Seema. Mother Munesh Rani says that her daughter Seema, brother-in-law Sanjeev Kumar Chaudhary, sister-in-law's father Rajendra Rana, Gambhir, and Naresh Kumar conspired together to seize her land. My daughter opened my bank account without permission to hide her 'black money'. She deposited ₹15 lakh into the account. When I found out and protested, she threatened to kill me. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to DSO Dr. Seema about the allegations. Read the full interview Question: Has an FIR been filed against you in Saharanpur? Answer: I came to know by reading the news that an FIR has been filed against me in Saharanpur district. I had no information about this before, nor has there ever been any dispute with my family. I keep talking to my mother. My photos and other information were also picked up and made viral everywhere and given to the media. My uncle Sanjeev Chaudhary's name is also included in this FIR. Question: What is the real dispute in the family? Answer: My father, Mahipal Singh, is a farmer by profession. He is 65 years old. Due to heart surgery and other illnesses, he remains unwell. My grandmother is also still alive. We still have a joint family. Instead of transferring my grandfather's share of land to my father's name, the family transferred it to my mother Munnesh's name. My mother Munnesh has 32 bighas of land in her name. My mother sold 17 bighas of land, which was in her name, to Anupam Joshi of Dehradun. This land is very expensive and was sold at a rate of 4 lakh rupees per bigha. That money must have come into my mother's account. The family went to court against this land sale, and the case is currently ongoing in court. Question: How did the land dispute arise? Answer: Among us four sisters, there is one brother, and the family sent him abroad for studies. The family spent money on his education. Mom said I need to give more money to my son, to which we replied ‘the money given so far is already too much’. We don't know what happened to that money. Once you go abroad, you can even see it. MBA studies do not cost that much. On this, Mom started saying that I will sell the land and give the money to my son. This is where the dispute started. Mom secretly sold the land at very cheap prices. Question: Why was an FIR filed against you? Answer: Mom started feeling that I am an officer and opposed the sale of the land. The land that has been sold is still under the family's possession. Anupam Joshi, who fraudulently bought the land, wants to take possession, but the matter is currently in court. My uncle Sanjeev Chaudhary said that we will give the amount for which the land was purchased, the land is ours. The land buyer is now asking for 18 lakh rupees per bigha for the land. That's probably why mom filed an FIR against me. Question: Your mother alleges that you deposited black money into her account? Answer: The bank account mentioned is mom's own bank account. I have not deposited any money into it. The bank opens an account after a full investigation and seeing the customer in person. Mom herself completed the KYC. In that account, ₹10 lakh were UPI transferred by maternal grandfather Rajendra Rana and ₹5 lakh by Sanjeev Chaudhary. Mom had also asked for this money for my brother abroad. The truth will come out in the bank investigation. Question: Did the police call you to Saharanpur? Answer: The police neither called me nor recorded my statement. My mother submitted an application letter. My name and DSO post are written in the very first line of it. The police should have known the truth. I should have been asked about the whole matter. Now I have told the police and administrative officers the truth of the whole matter. An attempt was made to tarnish my image without knowing the truth. Know the profile of the DSO's family

stories.title: Heavy rain hits Lucknow and 5 cities, water enters houses:Rain alert issued for all 75 UP districts; hail and lightning likely
stories.summary: The monsoon has now covered the entire state of Uttar Pradesh. At around 3 am on Friday, heavy rain lashed 5 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Unnao and Jalaun. Cloudy skies have been reported in more than 30 cities, including Agra and Mathura, with sunshine appearing intermittently. By 6 am, Unnao had received so much rainfall that streets were waterlogged. Rainwater entered several houses. It has been raining continuously since 7 am in Jalaun. In Kanpur, at around 10 am on Thursday, a drain connected to a sewage treatment plant burst, flooding roads and affecting 12 nearby villages. A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Heavy rainfall is likely in 11 districts. Warnings have also been issued for hailstorms and lightning. Winds may blow at speeds of up to 40 kmph, with gusts reaching 50 kmph in some places. Earlier, on Thursday, rainfall was recorded in around 30 cities, including Lucknow and Kanpur. Strong winds swept through Varanasi. In Shamli, potholes appeared on the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway after the season's first rain. A mother and her eight-month-old daughter were swept away in the strong flow of a drain in Sonbhadra. In Ballia and Fatehpur, two people died after being struck by lightning. See the rain pictures- Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon has become active in Uttar Pradesh. There is now a possibility of continuous rainfall. The temperature has dropped by up to 8 °C. The weather is expected to remain the same for the next one week. However, during the monsoon season, Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, is likely to receive below-normal rainfall." 54% more rainfall than normal in the last 24 hrs; Sambhal and Mirzapur receive highest Uttar Pradesh recorded an average of 8.4 mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours, while the normal average rainfall for this period is 5.5 mm. This means the state received 54% more rainfall than normal. However, from 1 June to 2 July 2026, the state has received a total of 58.3 mm of rainfall, against the normal figure of 106.8 mm for the same period. This means Uttar Pradesh has so far recorded 45% below-normal rainfall. In the last 24 hours, Sambhal recorded the highest rainfall at 46.3 mm, followed by Mirzapur (43.9 mm), Azamgarh (41.3 mm), Badaun (29.8 mm), Moradabad (24.8 mm), Varanasi (20.9 mm), Hardoi (19.6 mm), Bijnor and Etah (18.7 mm each), and Lakhimpur Kheri (18.4 mm).

stories.title: Container runs over passengers in Etah, 5 dead:Roadways bus broke down, bodies left scattered on road
stories.summary: An out-of-control container ran over passengers of a roadways bus. 5 people died in the accident in Etah on Thursday at around 11:30 PM. 12 people were injured. The bus was going from Etah to Delhi with 40 passengers. According to eyewitnesses, the roadways bus had broken down and was standing on the roadside. Some passengers had gotten off the bus and were standing outside due to the heat. Just then, a speeding container came and, crushing everyone, hit the bus from behind, then went to the other side of the road. The bodies of passengers were scattered on the road. After the accident, there was chaos and screaming. Local people and police sent the injured to Veerangana Avantibai Medical College, where doctors declared five people dead. The accident occurred in the Bagwala police station area. See 2 pictures related to the accident- Women and children were sitting inside the bus, so they survived On receiving information about the accident, DM Arvind Singh and SSP Dr. Ilamaran reached the spot and gathered information about the accident. A traffic jam had occurred at the spot due to the accident. The police cleared the jam by removing the bus and container with a crane. The deceased have been identified as Satendra (38), a resident of Bulandshahr, Rajesh (34), Sukhram (30) and Shailesh (29) from Farrukhabad. One person could not be identified. Women, children and elderly people remained seated inside the bus, so nothing happened to them. Pawan Kumar, brother of the deceased Rajesh, said that the bus was parked on the roadside due to a breakdown. Meanwhile, a speeding container coming from behind hit it. His younger brother was going to Delhi with the family's two daughters. DM Arvind Singh said that the bus was standing on the roadside due to a breakdown, but some part of it was on the road. Meanwhile, a container coming from behind hit the bus, due to which the passengers standing outside came under its grip. The injured are being given better treatment. stories.title: Who will be SP's new chief whip?:After Kamal Akhtar, will Akhilesh back a Muslim, Dalit or Kurmi leader?
stories.summary: SP's Assembly Chief Whip Kamal Akhtar resigned from his post. The big question is, whom will Akhilesh Yadav entrust with this important responsibility now? Akhilesh's decision will also set SP's caste formula for the 2027 elections. Akhilesh options He can maintain Muslim representation. He can further sharpen the 'PDA' formula. He can bring in a non-Yadav OBC face. In such a situation, he has 3 main types of contenders. Let's understand the political strength of these faces. Option 1- Strong Muslim Face If the Chief Whip is a Muslim face, SP's grip on the minority vote bank will strengthen further in 2027. SP's strongest base has been Muslim-Yadav (M-Y). However, if SP makes this decision, BJP will once again get an opportunity to accuse them of appeasement. Know the potential faces Option 2- Sharpening PDA with a Dalit Face After the success of the PDA formula in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP wants to send a big message to Dalits. Therefore, it is believed that the party high command can put forward a Dalit face for the chief whip. This could be SP's masterstroke to attract the backward vote bank. Know the Potential Faces Option 3- Damage to BJP from a non-Yadav OBC face The influence of the Kurmi community has rapidly increased in UP politics. To infiltrate this strong fortress of BJP and to show that SP is not limited to just the M-Y factor, SP can put forward a non-Yadav OBC face. Know the potential faces On July 2, Akhilesh Yadav said on Kamal Akhtar's resignation that only those parties run whose decisions are accepted by their leaders. Kamal Akhtar is our old worker and leader. At one time, he was the youngest Rajya Sabha MP. He is very sensible. Chief Whip - From coordination to setting the party line The role of the Chief Whip inside the assembly is very important. Ensuring the presence of party MLAs, enforcing the whip (party line) during voting, determining legislative strategy, and coordinating with opposition parties are his responsibilities. However, according to some senior SP leaders, this post is also a kind of 'headache' - SP leaders say - the chief whip is not just a post for maintaining caste balance. Akhilesh needs a face with acceptance in the organization to strategize against the government inside the assembly and keep the MLAs united. Someone who can communicate with all factions. Caste equations alone cannot be the sole basis for this appointment. However, in view of the preparations for 2027, Akhilesh's decision will certainly determine the party's future direction. Why did Chief Whip Kamal Akhtar resign? Dispute between MP Ruchiveera and Kamal Akhtar The souring of relations between Kamal Akhtar and Ruchi Veera has been ongoing since the Lok Sabha elections (2024). However, the matter was being handled internally until now. This discord came to the surface when the PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) Honour Conference was held in Moradabad on June 14. In this, MP Ruchi Veera was neither invited nor was her photo displayed at the event. Ruchi Veera became angry about this. The national president called an emergency meeting on June 25. MP Ruchi Veera, Rajya Sabha MP Javed Ali, former minister Kamal Akhtar, and former MLA Yusuf Ansari were present. In the meeting, Ruchi Veera said- Kamal Akhtar opposes me in Moradabad. He is creating factionalism in the party. Kamal Akhtar himself did not allow my photo to be displayed at the PDA conference. This gave the BJP and its allies an opportunity to say that women are not respected in the SP. Kamal Akhtar had accused Ruchi Veera of factionalism. Kamal had said that ever since Ruchi Veera became an MP, she does not allow photos of any MLA or SP leader on her hoardings. When she doesn't put anyone's photo, why would anyone put her photo? Following this, SP MLA Kamal Akhtar from Kanth assembly constituency of Moradabad resigned from the post of Chief Whip of the legislature on June 30. Kamal Akhtar reached Lucknow at 2:30 PM. He met party president Akhilesh Yadav at the party headquarters and handed over his resignation. Kamal Akhtar wanted to contest Lok Sabha elections from Moradabad The root cause of the rift between Kamal Akhtar and Ruchi Veera is the Moradabad Lok Sabha seat. Kamal Akhtar is counted among Akhilesh Yadav's close and trusted leaders. Kamal Akhtar, who has been a minister in the Akhilesh government, has also previously served as an SP Rajya Sabha MP. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Kamal Akhtar wanted to contest from the Moradabad seat. Akhilesh Yadav had also given him the party symbol. But, at the last moment, due to SP leader Azam Khan's veto, Akhilesh had to take back the symbol from Kamal Akhtar and give it to Ruchi Veera. Ruchi Veera wants to field her daughter MP Ruchi Veera wants to field her daughter Swati Veera from the Moradabad city seat in 2027. Swati Veera has contested the Nagar Panchayat election from Bijnor, but she lost. Became Chief Whip after Manoj Pandey turned rebel SP had made Kamal Akhtar its Chief Whip in the UP Assembly on July 28, 2024. Before him, Raebareli MLA Manoj Kumar Pandey was the Chief Whip. However, Manoj resigned from the post of Chief Whip in February 2024, adopting an anti-party stance during the Rajya Sabha elections. He had voted in favor of BJP candidates. This post became vacant only after he changed sides. Kamal Akhtar was later appointed to this post.

stories.title: Govt sends notice to Telegram over pirated films, shows
stories.summary: Authorities have issued a stern notice to Telegram, demanding proactive measures against the rampant circulation of pirated films and shows. The government insists the messaging app must go beyond individual channel takedowns and implement robust systems to detect and remove infringing content. This move follows previous concerns regarding Telegram's use for illegal activities, including fraud and the distribution of harmful material. An action report is expected within fifteen days.

stories.title: Monsoon session from July 20, govt hopes to push key bills in Parliament
stories.summary: The government aims to reintroduce its ambitious women's reservation bill in the upcoming monsoon session after a previous defeat. Speaker Om Birla's decision on defecting MPs could bolster the ruling alliance's numbers. Discussions are also expected on potential changes to the bill to address concerns from southern states, alongside a proposal for automatic removal of leaders facing serious criminal charges.

stories.title: India bucking trend by adding refining capacity: PM Modi
stories.summary: Amidst global energy turmoil, India, under PM Modi's leadership, bolstered domestic LPG output and secured diverse crude supplies. Strategic diplomacy and policy interventions successfully shielded citizens from potential shortages and price surges. The inauguration of the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery marks a significant step in India's expanding refining prowess, positioning it as the world's fourth-largest refining nation.

stories.title: Carmakers on E20: No engine damage, but mileage drops
stories.summary: Vehicle manufacturers are defending the government's mandatory 20% ethanol blending in petrol, assuring the public that no engine damage has been observed. While acknowledging a slight drop in fuel efficiency for older vehicles due to lower calorific value, industry leaders state field experience has been positive. Discussions are ongoing with the government regarding flex-fuel vehicles as a future pathway.

stories.title: As vehicles get smarter, govt plans to thwart hijackings, roll out software update norms
stories.summary: India's road transport ministry is introducing mandatory cybersecurity and software update rules for advanced vehicles. Starting October, new models with Level-3 automation and above will need to comply, followed by existing models and then vehicles with over-the-air update capabilities. This proactive measure addresses the growing threat of cyberattacks on increasingly connected cars, ensuring safer journeys for all.

stories.title: MHA tags 17 from Pakistan and 6 Indians 'individual terrorists'
stories.summary: India has declared 23 individuals from Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir as terrorists, targeting Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish operatives. Home Minister Amit Shah stated these individuals are involved in anti-India activities, including terror attacks and recruitment. The designated terrorists are linked to significant attacks like Pathankot and the Rameshwaram Cafe blast, with some also involved in reconnaissance for future strikes. This move underscores the government's firm stance against terrorism.

stories.title: BJP splitting parties, but won't get 2/3rd majority, says Congress
stories.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh has accused the BJP of attempting to split opposition parties ahead of the monsoon session, warning that their true aim is to alter India's Constitution. Despite efforts, Ramesh asserted the ruling party will not achieve the two-thirds majority needed for such a move, citing the 'Ab ki Baar, 400 Paar' slogan's failure. He anticipates bills like delimitation and 'One Nation, One Election' might be introduced.

12k pilgrims visit Amarnath; 3rd batch of 4.8k leave for ice Shivling darshan
stories.summary: Thousands of pilgrims are continuing their journey to the sacred Shri Amarnath cave shrine. On Saturday, the third batch of 4,812 devotees departed from Jammu's Yatri Niwas base camp. This follows a successful opening day where over 12,000 pilgrims offered prayers. The administration has made advance registration compulsory, and helicopter services are unavailable due to the no-fly zone declaration along the pilgrimage route.

AAI withdraws Srinagar airport closure for repairs, Omar Abdullah thanks govt
stories.summary: Srinagar airport's planned Monday-Tuesday closures and a full shutdown from October 1-16 have been withdrawn by AAI. The Indian Air Force had proposed these closures for runway repairs. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expressed gratitude for the government's prompt response, highlighting the importance of uninterrupted air connectivity for tourism and the region's economy, especially during peak holiday seasons.

stories.title: PoK 'infiltrator' saved by love, sent back home
stories.summary: A young man from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, Zeeshan Mir, was repatriated home after crossing the Line of Control to meet his beloved, Iram Bano. Initially detained, Mir was eventually acquitted by an Uri court, which recognized his act as a desperate attempt of love rather than infiltration. The couple, whose families are related across the border, shared a brief meeting before Mir's handover, with both families hoping for their union.

stories.title: 'Anti-national' school library book rocks J&K, 8 officials suspended
stories.summary: A political uproar has erupted in Jammu and Kashmir following the discovery of books in government school libraries describing the region as "India-occupied Kashmir" and referring to a banned separatist leader as "Shaheed." The BJP has demanded the education minister's resignation, while the administration has suspended officials, blacklisted publishers, and launched a high-level inquiry into the matter. This incident reignites the ongoing debate over narratives in the region.

stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar is embarking on a significant six-nation tour from July 5-15, commencing with a visit to four Gulf countries to bolster bilateral ties and discuss regional matters. He will then head to New York to spearhead India's campaign for a UN Security Council seat. The tour concludes in Brussels for crucial India-EU Trade and Technology Council discussions, underscoring India's proactive diplomatic outreach.

'Knows who the boss is': Trump says Netanyahu requested White House meeting next week
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu requested a White House meeting, potentially next week. Trump highlighted their strong relationship, despite recent reports of differing views on regional issues like Iran and Lebanon. The visit, if confirmed, would be significant for Netanyahu ahead of Israel's upcoming elections. Trump also commented on Iran's eagerness for a deal and the funeral of former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

stories.summary: BJP National General Secretary Tarun Chugh held a crucial meeting with Union Home Minister Amit Shah to address escalating issues in Punjab, including rising lawlessness, cross-border terrorism, and drug trafficking. Chugh is optimistic about the BJP's potential to bring transformative governance, security, and growth to Punjab post-2027 Assembly elections, aiming to restore stability and prosperity in the region.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Bill Clinton: “If you live long enough, you'll make mistakes. But if you learn from them, you'll be a better person. It's how you handle adversity, not how it affects you. The main thing is never quit, never quit, never quit.”
'Historical necessity to make Rahul Gandhi PM': Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
'Divine retribution against US, Israel not far off': Iran fires new warning as Khamenei funeral begins
Security forces launch major anti-terror operation in J&K's Shopian
stories.summary: On Saturday, security forces launched a substantial anti-terror operation in the Meemandar area of Shopian, triggered by credible intelligence regarding militant activity. The team is currently conducting an exhaustive cordon and search process, diligently exploring the region. According to officials, this operation began based on targeted inputs, and more information will be revealed as the search progresses.

stories.title: 'Iran mourns 40,000 killed by Khamenei, not him': Exiled crown prince calls funeral 'propaganda'
Did Zohran Mamdani sit on the wrong side of George Washington's desk? Billionaire Bill Ackman says it's evident the NYC mayor has never held any job
America@250: The United States of Anxiety
Too hot for a cold one: How European heatwave is impacting alcohol consumption?
'Sought by MPs across party lines': Speaker Om Birla says report on Justice Yashwant Varma to be tabled in Monsoon Session
stories.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla announced that the probe committee's report on Justice Yashwant Varma will be presented during the upcoming Monsoon Session, following requests from MPs across parties. Justice Varma resigned in April after facing impeachment proceedings due to the recovery of burnt currency notes from his residence. The report's tabling marks a significant step in the ongoing process.

stories.title: 'How long will govt ignore our voices': Dipke writes to PM Modi as protest enters Day 15
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding he address education activist Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged exam irregularities. The protest, now in its 15th day, highlights concerns over repeated exam leaks and student suicides, with Dipke criticizing the government's silence and alleged mistreatment of protesters.

stories.title: Hubble has spotted ‘impossible’ light in deep space, and scientists are trying to explain where it came from
stories.summary: Astronomers have spotted a remarkably small yet potent galaxy, MXDFz4. 4, from the universe's nascent stages. This galaxy, observed by Hubble and confirmed by other powerful telescopes, is emitting energetic ultraviolet light, a phenomenon previously thought impossible for its era. This discovery offers an unprecedented glimpse into how early galaxies began to clear the cosmic fog, paving the way for light to travel freely.

stories.title: 3 acquitted of 2019 murder of Irish journalist Lyra McKee shot while covering Northern Ireland riots
'Ended the same war so many times': Biden Jr. mocks Trump, names him for Peace Prize
'May next 250 years bring greater peace & progress': PM Modi congratulates Trump on US Independence Day
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended warm wishes to US President Donald Trump and the American people on their 250th Independence Day. He emphasized the shared democratic values and the strength of the India-US partnership, expressing optimism for its future growth and prosperity. The US marked this significant milestone with nationwide festivities, celebrating its founding and democratic ideals.

stories.title: Bareilly Cantonment becomes carbon-negative, first in India
China's pawn in the Middle East? : How Beijing 'uses' Pakistan to sell weapons
Delhi Gymkhana Club challenges Centre's eviction proceedings in HC, plea listed for July 6
stories.summary: The Delhi Gymkhana Club and its staff are challenging the government's eviction notice in the Delhi High Court. The Centre initiated proceedings after terminating the club's perpetual lease, deeming its continued occupation of the 27.3-acre Lutyens' Delhi property an "unauthorised occupation." The government claims the land is needed for defence and public-interest projects, but the club contests the termination and eviction order.

stories.title: 'I want this on Donald's desk by August recess': Melania Trump gives Congress private deadline to pass her bill
King Charles sends warm wishes to Trump on America's 250th Independence Day
'Academic jihad': BJP seeks ban on J&K textbook 'glorifying terrorists'; LG suspends 8
stories.summary: The Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir has taken decisive action by suspending officials and initiating an inquiry into school library books deemed to contain 'inappropriate content.' This decision comes after reports surfaced of a book that seemingly glorified terrorists and separatists while promoting a harmful narrative. Consequently, authors and publishers face blacklisting, and the distribution of such publications is being halted across the Union Territory.

stories.title: Scientists have found a billion-year-old hidden magma system on Mars that supported life on the Red planet
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence of a massive magma system beneath Mars' surface, challenging the long-held belief that such complex geological activity requires tectonic plates. NASA's InSight lander data revealed a distinct boundary deep within the Martian crust, suggesting a vast, ancient magma chamber that cooled and crystallized. This discovery hints that the ingredients for life might be more common on Mars than previously thought, prompting a re-evaluation of planetary habitability.

stories.title: A Maine couple thought they were about to photograph a moose. Instead, a calf and a bear burst from the woods, and they had seconds to decide whether to intervene
stories.summary: A peaceful fishing trip in Maine took a dramatic turn when Todd and Elvia Malcolm witnessed a black bear pursuing a moose calf. Reacting swiftly, Todd drove his truck between the predator and its prey, startling the bear and allowing the calf to escape to its mother. Elvia, meanwhile, captured the heart-pounding moments on her phone, unknowingly documenting the incredible rescue

stories.title: Proverb of the day: 'Rahiman dhaga prem ka' – Rahim's timeless lesson on relationships and why trust, once broken, is never the same
stories.summary: Centuries-old wisdom from poet Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana highlights the fragility of trust in relationships. His famous doha warns against impulsive anger, comparing love to a delicate thread that, once broken, can be mended but will always bear a knot. This timeless advice remains crucial in today's fast-paced digital world, urging us to prioritize patience and understanding to preserve precious bonds.

stories.title: Why did Keir Starmer leave 10 Downing Street? Former UK PM opens up on 'intensely personal' decision
stories.summary: Keir Starmer revealed his decision to step down as Labour leader and Prime Minister was a deeply personal one, made with his family at Chequers. He emphasized the need for his successor to navigate ongoing global and domestic challenges, defending his record of rebuilding the party. Starmer plans to remain an MP but will refrain from advising his successor, aiming to ensure the next government's success.

stories.title: 'Join BJP and take on me': Mamata Banerjee challenges TMC 'traitors', takes over as Bengal unit chief
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee has challenged rebel leaders to join the BJP directly, accusing the saffron party of instigating dissent. She questioned their timing, asking why their grievances weren't raised during their long tenures as TMC representatives. Banerjee emphasized the loyalty of party workers and warned rebels against betraying voters. This comes as Chandrima Bhattacharya, recently appointed state unit chief, joined the dissident faction.

stories.title: Why India is planning Namo Cities—and what they could mean for Delhi-NCR
stories.summary: India is embarking on a massive urban transformation, planning to build new cities around high-speed transit to accommodate a projected population surge in the National Capital Region. These "Namo Cities," part of Regional Plan-2041, will be developed as Transit-Oriented Developments, integrating housing, jobs, and services around Namo Bharat RRTS stations.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: PM Modi launches major infra projects in Rajasthan; TMC faces another setback
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated development projects worth Rs 1.06 lakh crore in Rajasthan, including a new Jodhpur Airport terminal. Meanwhile, TMC leader Chandrima Bhattacharya resigned from all party posts. The Centre designated 23 Pakistan-based operatives as terrorists under UAPA. Raj Thackeray criticized the BJP's 'arrogance with power,' targeting CM Fadnavis. All eyes are on young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's potential India debut ahead of the 2nd T20I.

stories.title: Muslim nurse in Texas says she won't treat anyone watching Fox News; university ensures she doesn't have to, fires her after probe
'BJP taking over our offices across Bengal': Mamata faction's Saugata Roy after rebels 'lock' TMC's Kolkata premises
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Saugata Roy accused the BJP of orchestrating a takeover of party offices across West Bengal, following a rebel faction's seizure of the Kolkata headquarters. Roy dismissed the rebel leader's claims, stating the incident reflects a broader BJP strategy to undermine the TMC. He vowed the party would continue its political struggle despite these challenges, emphasizing the ongoing fight for control.

stories.title: The empire of doubt, ally of convenience: America at 250, seen from India
Proverb of the day: 'Kal kare so aaj kar, aaj kare so ab' - a timeless lesson for the lazy by Sant Kabir and why one should prioritise work
stories.summary: Sant Kabir's timeless wisdom, urging immediate action over delay, resonates powerfully today amidst digital distractions. His famous doha, "Kal kare so aaj kar, aaj kare so ab," highlights life's uncertainty and the risks of procrastination. This ancient advice, far from promoting haste, champions decisive action, reminding us that the present moment is our only guarantee, not a distant, uncertain tomorrow.

stories.title: 'Became difficult to continue working': Chandrima Bhattacharya explains TMC exit; party calls move 'pre-planned'
stories.summary: Chandrima Bhattacharya resigned from all Trinamool Congress posts, citing a loss of confidence from party chief Mamata Banerjee. Bhattacharya rejected claims of disloyalty, stating her decision stemmed from a phone call where Banerjee blamed her for the rebel faction's takeover of the party office. This move follows the TMC's internal crisis and a significant electoral defeat.

stories.title: Antarctica is missing 2 million sq km of sea ice, scientists say the impact may reach far beyond the frozen continent
stories.summary: New research reveals Antarctica's significant, underestimated role in global warming. A study highlights a stronger link between Antarctic sea ice, cloud cover, and Earth's heat storage than previously thought. This suggests the planet may be more sensitive to greenhouse gas emissions, potentially leading to faster warming and more severe climate impacts globally. Urgent emission reductions are crucial to mitigate these risks.

stories.title: Celebratory firing death case: Bihar BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh convicted, gets 4-year jail
stories.summary: A Delhi court has sentenced Bihar BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh to four years imprisonment and a Rs 25 lakh fine for culpable homicide in a 2018 celebratory firing case. The incident tragically claimed the life of Archana Gupta during a New Year's party. The court emphasized the severe dangers of such reckless gunfire, with eyewitnesses identifying Singh as the shooter. The substantial fine will compensate the victim's family.

stories.title: BJP approaches EC over alleged interference in Karnataka voter roll revision
stories.summary: A BJP delegation led by state president BY Vijayendra, along with senior MLA and former minister S Suresh Kumar, met the Chief Electoral Officer on Saturday and submitted a formal complaint over the issue. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Vijayendra alleged that the Election Commission had launched the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls with the right intent, but the state government was attempting to disrupt the exercise.

stories.title: 'Why is theft happening in BJP-ruled states?' : Congress targets BJP over alleged donation theft at Kedarnath, Badrinath
stories.summary: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh has slated the BJP for alleged financial misconduct involving the Kedarnath and Badrinath temple trusts. He claims instances of donation misappropriation and raises concerns over governance in BJP-ruled regions. Emphasizing the significance of the Ram Temple campaign, he argues that such actions tarnish Ram’s legacy.

stories.title: Sikh man Vickrum Digwa seeks to appeal conviction in Henry Nowak murder case
Workplace harassment in Pakistan: 521 men filed complaints, transgenders and women also seek redress
Samyukta Kisan Morcha, which led farm laws protest, to join CJP's stir on Sunday
stories.summary: The SKM also expressed its "deepest sympathies" to students and families affected by what it described as the Modi government's "chronic paper leaks and examination mismanagement". "Every student has the right to a transparent, fair and credible system of education and examinations. Ensuring accountability in this regard is the responsibility of the government," the letter said.

stories.title: 'Demanded $100,000 for our release': Pakistan gang rape victim names deputy PM Ishaq Dar's kin
stories.summary: A cryptocurrency dispute is now central to the investigation of an alleged kidnapping and gang rape of two foreign women in Pakistan. One victim claims Raza Dar, a relative of the deputy prime minister, demanded $100,000 for their release after they were held captive and sexually assaulted. Investigators are exploring if Dar lured the women to Pakistan for a $1.5 million crypto deal, staging the abduction to appear genuine.

stories.title: Doctor, engineer… or something else? How India’s career dream is changing
stories.summary: In India, engineering and medicine have long been the cornerstones of middle-class aspirations, symbolizing security and respect. Yet, the landscape is transforming. With the rise of AI and digital sectors, the job market now prizes flexibility and contemporary skills over old-fashioned degrees. Professions in AI, cybersecurity, and digital marketing are emerging as attractive, rewarding alternatives to traditional paths, proving that the definition of success has evolved.

stories.title: 'Will fight for Punjab together': Warring plays down rift with Channi ahead of polls
stories.summary: Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring has dismissed rumours of internal party rifts, assuring that senior leaders will soon unite. He addressed speculation about replacing him with Charanjit Singh Channi, stating that Channi remains a respected leader and meetings among party members are normal. Warring emphasized that indiscipline would not be tolerated and that unity would be showcased soon for the upcoming elections.

stories.title: ECI issues notice to K Kavitha over use of 'TRS' in her new party's name: Report
stories.summary: The Election Commission of India has issued a notice to K Kavitha regarding her new party's name, Telangana Rakshana Sena. This follows over 1,100 complaints, including one from her former party, BRS, citing similarity to the erstwhile TRS. Despite accepting a name change, Kavitha retained the "TRS" initials, stating twenty years of their efforts were invested in that identity and the formation of Telangana state.

stories.title: ‎Which countries allow foreigners to adopt children? Here's what the rules look like
stories.summary: International adoption landscapes are shifting dramatically. Many nations now prioritize domestic placements, making cross-border adoptions a last resort. Countries like China have ended programs for non-relatives, while others, including India and Vietnam, maintain regulated systems. Prospective parents face longer waits and stricter scrutiny globally as rules tighten, reflecting a growing emphasis on child welfare within their home countries

stories.title: 'Men too can be victims': Rajya Sabha MP introduces National Commission for Men Bill in Parliament after Siya-Ketan case
'Up to 3,000 dead would be okay': Iran braces for mass casualties at Khamenei's funeral; report
China's Xi Jinping promotes two PLA generals after anti-corruption purge thins top military ranks
stories.summary: China's leader, Xi Jinping, has made notable advancements by promoting two military officials to generals, marking a pivotal change in the People's Liberation Army's hierarchy. Following rigorous anti-corruption efforts that reshaped the leadership structure, these promotions are essential for restoring loyalty and filling key positions within the Central Military Commission, setting the stage for a comprehensive reorganization prior to the forthcoming Communist Party congress.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu sends 50 Bangladeshi nationals to Bengal for deportation
stories.summary: Police said the group consists of 44 men and six women who had been lodged at the special detention camp inside the Attur taluk office complex in Salem district. After deportation orders were issued, they were taken from the camp to Tiruchirappalli by road in three police vans on July 3 under tight security arrangements.

stories.title: This toad exists only in Canada—and scientists have finally discovered why
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a genetically unique western toad population exclusively in Canada, a finding that could be more distinctively Canadian than native wildlife. This rare group, found in the Rockies, highlights the importance of conserving unique genetic diversity. The research reveals deeper genetic divisions within the species, emphasizing that even common animals can harbor irreplaceable natural heritage.

stories.title: UK parents urged not to share children's photos publicly over AI-enabled child abuse risks
'Made right decision at every level': PM Modi says 'diplomacy and dosti' helped India to tackle energy crisis
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted how India's strong international friendships and diplomacy were crucial in navigating the 21st century's biggest energy crisis, exacerbated by Middle East conflicts. He noted India expanded fuel imports to over 40 nations from 25-26, prioritizing national interest and citizen welfare. Modi also inaugurated Rajasthan's first integrated refinery, criticizing past government inaction on the project.

stories.title: 'Transgression': BJP meets Tamil Nadu governor over 2 'private individuals' at CM Vijay's official meeting, seeks action
Monsoon Session 2026 to begin on July 20, Parliament to sit until August 13
'Cruelty at its peak': PoJK leader seeks support of Indians in protest against Pakistan
stories.summary: A video message by Sardar Aman Khan, a core member of the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), has gone viral on social media. In the video, he calls upon people in Kashmir, Jammu, Ladakh, Poonch and Rajouri to stand in solidarity with residents of PoJK and participate in the July 5 protests, which have been planned across the region.

stories.title: Why houses in the Philippines stand on wooden stilts to survive floods, typhoons and extreme heat
'Absolute power corrupts': Raj Thackeray attacks BJP over 'insensitive' remarks on Mumbai deaths
stories.summary: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray has strongly criticized Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and the BJP, accusing them of arrogance and shielding colleagues who made insensitive remarks after two rain-related deaths in Mumbai. Thackeray lamented the decline of Maharashtra's political culture, urging Fadnavis to demand resignations from leaders behaving "shamelessly" to uphold the state's traditions.

stories.title: 'I don't think it is possible': Keir Starmer says next PM cannot spend less time on diplomacy
stories.summary: Outgoing British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has pushed back against criticism regarding his focus on international affairs, asserting that global diplomacy is intrinsically linked to domestic priorities. He argued that Britain's next leader will inevitably have to balance both, highlighting his government's role in restoring the UK's global standing and supporting Ukraine as key achievements.

stories.title: Centre puts Ram temple recce operative, Hafiz Saeed's son-in-law on terror list
stories.summary: ​​According to the ministry, he carried out reconnaissance of the Ram Janmabhoomi complex in Ayodhya, the RSS headquarters in Nagpur and the Indian Oil refinery in Panipat. He is also accused of serving as the launching commander for the Lasiyakot sector and facilitating infiltration through tunnels while arranging drone deliveries of arms and ammunition into India.

stories.title: The surprising amount of trash Americans generate on July 4 weekend
stories.summary: America's Fourth of July revelry leaves behind a staggering amount of waste, with over 120 million pounds of food and tons of fireworks debris littering public spaces. This colossal clean-up effort highlights significant food waste, particularly beef, and environmental costs. Coastal communities face immense challenges, with volunteers dedicating hours to clear beaches. The aftermath underscores the need for better planning to mitigate this annual post-celebration burden.

stories.title: 'Trump is your president': White house 'inserts' itself into Taylor Swift-Travis Kelce wedding celebrations
stories.summary: The White House playfully spoofed Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding announcement, altering a New York City billboard to read "Trump is your president." This social media jab follows Donald Trump's own Eras Tour-inspired graphic and his history of public criticism towards Swift, particularly after her endorsement of Kamala Harris. Despite past harsh words, Trump had offered a more positive sentiment regarding the couple's engagement.

stories.title: PM Modi launches India's first greenfield refinery, unveils Rs 1.06 lakh crore projects in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a new terminal at Jodhpur Airport and launched the Modified UDAN scheme. In Balotra, he dedicated projects worth Rs 1.06 lakh crore, including India's first greenfield integrated refinery-cum-petrochemical complex. He also handed over appointment letters to 54,000 Rajasthan government employees, emphasizing the government's commitment to project completion and self-reliance.

stories.title: 'They'll make someone scapegoat': Nana Patole accuses RSS-BJP of 'playing with Ram Temple devotees' sentiments'
Lady Louise’s graduation photos spark buzz as royal fans see young Queen Elizabeth II in her
stories.summary: The 22-year-old celebrated her St Andrews graduation before receiving the Duke of Edinburgh's Gold Award, but it was her striking resemblance to her late grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, that set social media abuzz.

stories.title: Fresh blow to TMC: West Bengal party president Chandrima Bhattacharya resigns
stories.summary: West Bengal's Trinamool Congress unit president Chandrima Bhattacharya has stepped down from all party positions amidst a wave of leaders departing the party. This development follows significant losses in the recent assembly elections and a subsequent organizational restructuring. The TMC has experienced internal divisions, with a notable split and a large contingent of Lok Sabha MPs joining a different party and aligning with the BJP-led NDA.

stories.title: US heat wave pushes power demand, triggers emergency electricity curbs and July 4 event disruptions
stories.summary: A severe heatwave gripping the eastern US has pushed electricity demand to near-record highs, forcing PJM Interconnection, the nation's largest power grid operator, to implement emergency measures. With generator issues and soaring air-conditioning needs, the grid is under immense strain, prompting calls for reduced consumption to avert blackouts. This extreme weather is also impacting July 4th celebrations and causing significant spikes in wholesale electricity prices.

stories.title: Ethiopia's Danakil Depression looks like another planet and scientists know exactly why
'TMC's internal matter': TMC leader Dilip Ghosh on rebel faction's takeover of party headquarters
stories.summary: A rebel faction of the Trinamool Congress, led by Ritabrata Banerjee, has seized control of the party's Kolkata headquarters, escalating an internal power struggle. West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh termed it an internal matter, stating the Speaker and law will decide office and seat occupancy. The Election Commission has set a July 6 deadline for both factions to submit claims, while police investigate building ownership.

stories.title: 'PM very angry': Congress says BJP splitting parties to 'take revenge' for Delimitation Bill setback
stories.summary: The Congress party accused the BJP of engaging in "revenge politics" after the Delimitation Bill failed to pass, alleging that Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Shah are orchestrating party splits. This comes as several leaders from Mamata Banerjee's TMC and Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena (UBT) have defected to rival factions, bolstering the BJP-led NDA.

stories.title: US summer heat: 5 cooling tricks people around world have used for generations
stories.summary: As record-breaking heatwaves grip the US and Europe, millions are seeking affordable ways to stay cool. Surprisingly, ancient wisdom from hotter climates offers effective solutions. From blocking sunlight and using water for natural cooling to wearing loose clothing and designing homes for airflow, these time-tested techniques are proving invaluable. Discover how centuries-old traditions are now guiding modern approaches to beat the heat

stories.title: Maharashtra deputy CM Eknath Shinde hospitalised due to fever & exhaustion
stories.summary: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was hospitalized Friday in Thane due to viral fever and exhaustion following a demanding political schedule. His condition is stable, with doctors attributing his illness to intense work and travel, including recent political maneuvers. The incident led to the postponement of a party event, which was later held with his son representing him.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Jodhpur airport's new terminal building, launches modified UDAN scheme
'Lift sanctions, we're ready to ... ': Iran's 'AC suggestion' to Europe amid heatwave
‘Honoured to welcome my friend’: Australian PM Albanese ahead of PM Modi’s visit next week
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese eagerly anticipates Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit to Melbourne from July 8-10. This meeting, part of Modi's three-nation tour, aims to bolster the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and Australia. Discussions will focus on deepening cooperation in trade, defense, security, and technology, reinforcing the Indo-Pacific's peace and prosperity. Albanese expressed honor in welcoming his "friend" Modi, highlighting the relationship's growing significance.

stories.title: Centre designates 23 Pakistan-based operatives linked to JeM, LeT as terrorists under UAPA - full list
stories.summary: India has officially declared 23 Pakistan-based individuals as terrorists under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. These individuals are linked to notorious terror outfits like Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba. The move empowers authorities to take stringent action against their terror networks and assets. Notably, Masood Ilyas Kashmiri, a senior JeM operative, was identified for his role in recruiting, training, and facilitating terror attacks, including the Sunjwan incident.

stories.title: Tiny coffin beside Ali Khamenei's: 14-month-old granddaughter honoured at Iran Supreme Leader's funeral
stories.summary: Iran mourned its late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei with funeral ceremonies in Tehran, where his coffin was displayed alongside that of his 14-month-old granddaughter, killed in an Israeli airstrike. The event also honored other family members, including his son-in-law and daughter. Thousands gathered for prayers, with traditional practices observed. The funeral procession is expected to span several days and locations, including neighboring Iraq.

stories.title: 'Lost 5kg weight, blood pressure and sugar level falling': Sonam Wangchuk's health update on Day 7 of hunger strike
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk, on his seventh day of hunger strike demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, has lost over 5 kilograms, with his blood pressure and sugar levels dropping. Abhijeet Dipke of Cockroach Janata Party urged the government to act and encouraged public support at Jantar Mantar. The protest, initiated over NEET irregularities, has garnered support from various political and civil society figures.

stories.title: Ram Temple donation case: Mastermind roped in kin, 200 handlers to run theft network, says report
stories.summary: A shocking investigation reveals a sophisticated racket masterminded to steal Ram temple donations. Employees were allegedly trained to siphon gold, silver, and material gifts, with a nephew and 200 external handlers involved. Precious metals were secretly transported for melting, bypassing local markets, while material donations like winter jackets were reportedly diverted and sold commercially. Key trust members were allegedly kept in the dark to facilitate the ongoing operation.

stories.title: NMC asks medical colleges to patent healthcare innovations
India plans global Ayurveda push to move beyond wellness image
Uttarakhand CM Dhami completes five years in office, credits PM Modi, 'double-engine govt' for state's progress
stories.summary: The Chief Minister said that under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and with the commitment of the Double Engine Government, several historic decisions have been taken over the past five years by giving the highest priority to development and the preservation of the state's cultural identity.

stories.title: 'Pradhan's birthday cake can't be baked with children's blood': Mahua Moitra joins CJP protest
Netanyahu, Donald Trump agree to meet in US soon after phone call
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump have agreed to meet soon in the United States following a phone call where Netanyahu lauded the strong bilateral ties. This planned meeting occurs amidst ongoing regional diplomatic efforts concerning Iran and Israel's continued military operations against Hezbollah. Notably, Netanyahu also expressed a desire for Israel to cease its reliance on US financial aid, citing the nation's economic growth.

stories.title: MP man's life sentence for killing wife reduced over 'can have 1,000 husbands like you' remark; HC calls it 'grave provocation'
'Fake news': Israel denies report it planned to assassinate Iranian negotiators
stories.summary: Israel has vehemently denied reports suggesting it planned to assassinate senior Iranian negotiators during diplomatic talks, labeling the claims "fake news." The New York Times report alleged US officials warned Iran of potential Israeli targeting of key figures like Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, fearing it would derail peace efforts. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump have agreed to a future meeting.

stories.title: 'Accountability in education': Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike enters day 7 with fresh appeal to govt
'They want us grateful for merely being allowed': Zohran Mamdani delivers pro-immigration July 4 speech
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani presented a pro-immigration vision of America, contrasting with President Trump's stance ahead of Independence Day. Speaking from City Hall, Mamdani, a naturalized citizen, emphasized immigration's centrality to the nation's identity and criticized exclusionary politics. He highlighted the contributions of immigrants and called for unity, asserting that America's strength lies in its continuous striving for ideals.

stories.title: 7 rescued as boat capsizes on Wisconsin lake; 3 children dead
stories.summary: A devastating storm on Geneva Lake, Wisconsin, led to a tragic boat capsizing, claiming three young lives and requiring the rescue of seven others. Powerful winds and rough waves overwhelmed the vessel carrying ten people, including children. The severe weather also caused widespread damage, power outages, and disrupted holiday weekend plans across the region.

stories.title: Australian officials ask fans to respect privacy of Neil, a 1000kg seal, who respects nothing
'Secret Service missed 102 radio calls during '24 Trump shooting'
'France, Belgium & The Netherlands saw 3,700 excess deaths in heatwave'
stories.summary: Europe's recent heatwave, spanning June 20-28, has resulted in an alarming 3,700 excess deaths across France, the Netherlands, and Belgium. France alone reported over 2,000 fatalities, with a significant rise in deaths among those over 45. Belgium and the Netherlands also registered hundreds of additional deaths, primarily affecting the elderly. Experts attribute this extreme heat to climate change, warning that initial figures may increase.

stories.title: Overnight lines to pay respects to Khamenei
stories.summary: Iran is mourning its slain supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with a week of funeral processions. His body lies in state in Tehran, drawing thousands of mourners and foreign dignitaries. The nation is united in grief and calls for vengeance following his death in a US and Israeli attack. The funeral marks a critical moment for Iran's leadership.

stories.title: 'No one is being shielded in Ayodhya donation case': VHP president Alok Kumar
